symbols.name: IRuntimePluginOptions
symbols.purpose: Symmetric plugin configuration combining a source and explicit Host exposure whitelist.
symbols.core:
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
Reuse actual Host integration and original channel resources; local callbacks retain acquisition, resolution and diagnostic ownership.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
Use the application’s paired protection functions on both endpoints. Encryption requires decrypt and the sign/verify pair for replay protection; signing alone needs verify. encodedType must describe the protected frame. Omit authentication only when the carrier’s trust policy permits it.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
Attach the application’s message probe when this connection needs diagnostic tracing; omit it for an unobserved connection.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Synchronous callback receives background or contained failures as error; no return is consumed, and failure handling stays with the original runtime reporter owner.
report.error: Original background or secondary failure supplied by the runtime owner.
No result is used; reporter errors are contained by the reporting boundary.
Omitted: defaultRpcReporter reports to console.error.
keyFactory: Advanced remote-proxy key callback returning an application string for automatically keyed retry paths. The direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read this inherited field itself.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
Supply local logical-key or retry policy only for the actual installed dispatch path; direct borrowed Peer dispatch may leave them unused.
retryPort: Advanced application-supplied retry dispatch port for remote-proxy paths; it receives the original retry input and returns the selected dispatch result. Direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read it itself.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
authentication.encrypt: Outbound sync/async encryption runs after the endpoint wraps its encoded value with replay metadata and before signing. Throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with its cause.
authentication.encrypt.value: Replay-bound authentication envelope produced by the endpoint, including its encoded payload; not the bare application payload.
authentication.encrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Encrypted value or its Promise, passed unchanged into sign.
Leave encrypt and decrypt out together when messages need signatures but not encryption. In that case, sign receives the unencrypted authentication envelope: the message data together with the information used to detect replay. Omitting encryption does not remove signing or verification.
authentication.decrypt: Inbound sync/async decryption runs on the value recovered by verify. The endpoint then validates the recovered authentication envelope and replay binding.
authentication.decrypt.value: Verified protected value returned by verify.
authentication.decrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Recovered replay-bound authentication envelope or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with the original cause.
Omit decrypt only when encrypt is also omitted. After verify checks the signature and recovers the inner value, the endpoint directly checks that value as the authentication envelope, including its replay information. It does not try to decrypt the value.
authentication.sign: Outbound sync/async signing runs after optional encryption and returns the complete protected frame representation. Signing and verification are required even without encryption.
authentication.sign.value: Encrypted value when encrypt exists, otherwise the replay-bound authentication envelope.
authentication.sign.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Signed representation or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Keep the declared encodedType output domain.
There is no default signing function. Provide sign together with verify whenever authentication is enabled. This remains required when encrypt and decrypt are configured: encryption alone is insufficient, and omitting sign rejects the configuration.
authentication.verify: Inbound sync/async verification receives the protected frame and must recover its authenticated inner value; returning a boolean is not a verification verdict protocol.
authentication.verify.value: Protected value received at the authentication pipeline edge.
authentication.verify.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Authenticated inner value or its Promise, passed to decrypt when configured; reject or throw on invalid signatures. Local reporting retains the original verification failure, which may be sensitive; the peer receives a sanitized summary. Other returned values still undergo envelope/replay validation.
There is no default verification function. Provide verify together with sign so incoming protected messages can be checked and their inner values recovered. If sign is supplied without verify, construction rejects the configuration before the endpoint becomes active.
authentication.encodedType: Declared protected-output domain must match the next physical pipeline edge. Encrypt/decrypt and sign/verify are complete pairs, at least signing is required, and encryption additionally requires signing.
any: do not impose a declared protected-output value category.
Leave the declared output domain unconstrained; transforms may still change representation.
Declare that the protected output is text for the subsequent pipeline edge.
Declare that the protected output is a byte array for the subsequent pipeline edge.
spawn: Application source callback receiving the safe local identity and capability offer; choose exactly one source.
spawn.context: IRuntimePeerSourceContext from this preparation, containing its self identity and actual offered capabilities; no public abort signal is added to this context.
Promise of a complete IRuntimePeerSourceResult with agreed pipeline and features; failure rejects construction and rolls back resources already acquired.
Omitting spawn means this Peer starts no execution unit through that source. Select connect to reach an existing peer, or listen to accept one; exactly one source is required.
Choose exactly one source input interpreted by the actual platform peer factory; preserve that factory’s acquisition semantics.
connect: Application source callback opening a channel to an existing peer; choose exactly one source.
connect.context: IRuntimePeerSourceContext from this preparation, containing its self identity and actual offered capabilities; no public abort signal is added to this context.
Omitting connect means no outgoing connection is opened through this source. Choose spawn to start a peer or listen to accept one instead; exactly one source is required.
listen: Application source callback accepting a negotiated peer channel; choose exactly one source.
listen.context: IRuntimePeerSourceContext from this preparation, containing its self identity and actual offered capabilities; no public abort signal is added to this context.
Omitting listen means this Peer does not accept incoming connections through this source. Choose spawn or connect for the initiating side; exactly one source is required.
name: Caller-selected nonempty registration name copied when constructing the cold plugin; use the same name when addressing the installed runtime outlet.
expose: Distinct nonempty paths explicitly exposing current Host feature methods, runtime connection routes or the reserved host control entry. Only this snapshotted whitelist becomes remotely callable.
Omitted: an empty whitelist; only provide methods are published.
host: The same actual PluginHost handle into which this plugin is installed, supplying use, unUse, plugin and revision for explicit host exposure.
Omitted: allowed unless expose contains host; explicit host exposure requires host, catalog and resolvePlugin together.
catalog: Application-authored IRemoteHostCatalog declaring the only plugin contracts available through explicitly exposed host control.
Omitted: no host-control catalog; required when expose contains host.
resolvePlugin: Synchronous local resolver invoked by the canonical host-control owner after catalog admission; definitions remain local and are installed through the original Host.
resolvePlugin.name: Plugin name admitted by the declared catalog.
resolvePlugin.config: Optional portable configuration from the remote host-use request.
Local plugin definition accepted by the Host; a thrown error rejects the host-use request.
Omitted: no local resolver; required when expose contains host.

members.description: Optional Host-control catalog used only when host is explicitly exposed.

members.name: resolvePlugin
members.description: Local synchronous resolver for explicitly exposed Host installation controls.

members.name: endpointFactory
members.description: A custom runtime assembly receives only the operations held by this channel view.

members.name: self
members.description: Optional local identity; omission generates an instance id with the display name peer.

members.name: provide
members.description: Explicit nested own-data method groups; defaults to no application methods and rejects accessors during compilation.

members.name: providerLimits
members.description: Provider quotas, defaulting to 256 global and 64 per verified peer.

members.name: authentication
members.description: Existing per-frame credentials enable signed native transfer without a custom endpoint.

members.name: probe
members.description: Installs an endpoint-local synchronous observer without changing pipeline selection.

members.name: defaultTimeoutMs
members.description: Only request/stream inherit this positive default in their original timeout scope.

members.name: contract
members.description: Explicit advanced schema, modes and idempotency retain their original contract owner.

members.name: keyFactory
members.description: Optional idempotency key generator; omission uses the canonical identity generator.

members.name: retryPort
members.description: Optional whole-invocation retry policy; omission sends once.

symbols.name: IRuntimeTypedPeer
symbols.purpose: A Runtime Peer typed by `TRemote`: method names, payloads and results are checked against the other side API. Also has `self`, `describe()`, `outcome()`, `on()` and `close()`.
symbols.core:
self: Frozen local peer name and instanceId minted or supplied during this connection construction; it is not a remote authentication principal.
outcome: Queries the original remote operation ledger for a prior idempotency key, without dispatching that operation again.
outcome.idempotencyKey: The caller-issued key supplied as options.idempotencyKey on an earlier request to this connection.
Promise of IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult; support and availability come from the accepted remote runtime contract.
describe: Queries the local accepted peer detail asynchronously. Without format returns IRuntimeDetail; json, yaml or toml returns the admitted text projection. It does not claim unavailable physical metrics.
describe.options: Optional query format from IRuntimeQueryOptions; omitted returns the object snapshot.
Promise of local detail or formatted text, following the selected query format.
on: Registers a future RuntimeEventName listener after construction; factory resolution already represents initial readiness. Listener return is ignored and failures are contained by the runtime reporter.
on.event: A RuntimeEventName value such as ready or exit; it selects future connection lifecycle notifications.
on.listener: Callback receives IRuntimeEvent from this connection; return is ignored and throws or rejected thenables are reported.
Idempotent removal function for this registration; closing the peer clears its publisher.
close: Ends this logical connection and releases its owned channel resources; platform factories also terminate a worker or child they spawned.
Shared completion Promise retaining the original close operation identity; no new calls are admitted once closing begins.
[Symbol.asyncDispose]: Scoped asynchronous cleanup is the exact original close operation, including its Promise identity.
The same completion Promise as close(), including platform-owned resource cleanup.
request: Calls a method the other side provides and waits for its result. Default deadline 30000 ms (`defaultTimeoutMs`); errors keep their native type and `(source, code)`.
request.method: Dotted path of a method in the other side `provide`, e.g. `math.double`.
request.args: `(payload?, options?)`: one payload and call options (`timeoutMs`, `signal`, `transfer`, `idempotencyKey`).
The method result, typed from `TRemote`.
notify: Sends a one-way call; no result comes back.
notify.method: Dotted method path provided by the other side.
notify.args: `(payload?, options?)` as for `request`.
Resolves once the call was sent.
stream: Calls a method that returns an iterable and yields its items as they arrive.
stream.method: Dotted path of an iterator method provided by the other side.
stream.args: `(payload?, options?)` as for `request`.
An async iterator of the yielded items.
group: Sends several calls as one batch and returns the outcome of each step in order.
group.steps: Steps `{ method, payload? }` in order.
group.options: Batch options such as `timeoutMs` and `signal`.
One outcome per step (success value or error).

symbols.name: RpcRemoteLayerErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Stable remote-layer errors and caller recovery actions.
symbols.core:
runtimeEventOverflow: More than 100 unread passive events; query current state and resubscribe.
contractInvalid: Description or control payload is invalid; correct it before retry.
hostNotAdopted: This connection lacks live adoption; perform host use before removal.
startFailed: Unit preparation or channel acquisition failed; inspect the cause.
closed: Registration was released or generation left; wait for valid readiness.
resultUnknown: A sent request lost its result after departure; reconcile before repeating a non-idempotent operation.

members.name: runtimeEventOverflow
members.description: A passive watch exceeded 100 unread events; query current state before subscribing again.

members.name: contractInvalid
members.description: A description or control payload violates the remote contract; correct it before retrying.

members.name: hostNotAdopted
members.description: HostUnUse, including dryRun, lacks this connection's live adoption of the same remotely * installed definition. Complete hostUse before removing it.

members.name: startFailed
members.description: A supervisor cannot provide a ready unit or a channel cannot open; inspect the cause.

members.name: closed
members.description: The registration was released or its generation left; wait for another ready generation.

members.name: resultUnknown
members.description: A sent request lost its result with the generation; reconcile before another non-idempotent * call.

blocks.text: 错误保留原生类型、message、stack 与 cause；错误形状用 IRpcError，平台/拓扑值域用 IRpcPlatformValue / IRpcTransportTopologyValue。按稳定 source/code 而非 message 分支，远端身份只作诊断，不授予本地控制权。

isRpcErrorInstance / isRpcRemoteError / isRpcTimeoutError 按稳定字段跨 realm/副本判断，不能依赖 instanceof；isRpcError 只检查字符串 code，不能替代错误族守卫。RpcError、RpcRemoteError、RpcTimeoutError 等仅类型导出，唯一公开可构造类为 RpcLifecycleError，供持有自身释放状态的消费方使用。

rows: TimeoutError / AbortError；结果可能未知，查账而非盲重试
准入拒绝，具体原因看提供方 onRejected
载体失败，已送达与否需对账

symbols.name: createMessageListenerHub
symbols.purpose: Creates a local listener fan-out hub sharing one physical attachment across distinct callback identities.
symbols.core:
Local hub with size, has(listener), add(listener, attach), remove(listener, detach), dispatch(message, invoke) and clear(detach). add/remove/clear return void except remove returning whether a member was removed; has returns boolean. Dispatch snapshots membership and propagates invoke failures. Attach/detach callbacks are synchronous; failure leaves the logical change uncommitted.

`size`: Current number of distinct registered callback identities.

`has`: Checks whether this exact callback is registered. `listener`: Original application callback passed to add. True only for a currently registered callback identity.

`add`: Attaches the physical listener before adding the first callback; duplicate callbacks remain one Set member. `listener`: Application callback to retain by identity. `attach`: Synchronous physical registration callback; a throw leaves this callback unregistered. No result; first successful attachment and membership are retained.

`remove`: Detaches before removing the last callback; a detach throw keeps membership so release can be retried. `listener`: Exact original callback supplied to add. `detach`: Synchronous physical removal callback invoked only for the last member. True if removed, false if absent; detach failure propagates.

`dispatch`: Snapshots callbacks before invocation; reentrant membership changes affect subsequent dispatches, and an invoke throw stops this dispatch. `message`: Actual message received from the physical carrier. `invoke`: Synchronous dispatcher receiving each snapshot listener and the message; use observeListener to isolate failures. No result; invokes each snapshot member unless the dispatcher throws.

`clear`: Detaches the physical listener before clearing all callbacks; failure keeps membership intact. `detach`: Synchronous physical removal callback. No result; membership is empty after successful return.

blocks.text: 错误保留原生类型、message、stack 与 cause；错误形状用 IRpcError，平台/拓扑值域用 IRpcPlatformValue / IRpcTransportTopologyValue。按稳定 source/code 而非 message 分支，远端身份只作诊断，不授予本地控制权。

isRpcErrorInstance / isRpcRemoteError / isRpcTimeoutError 按稳定字段跨 realm/副本判断，不能依赖 instanceof；isRpcError 只检查字符串 code，不能替代错误族守卫。RpcError、RpcRemoteError、RpcTimeoutError 等仅类型导出，唯一公开可构造类为 RpcLifecycleError，供持有自身释放状态的消费方使用。

symbols.purpose: Creates a bounded collector that is itself a Core probe. Install it through probePlugin to collect endpoint events; it retains scalar metadata immediately and converts query, watch and record results only at reader boundaries. It creates no Peer or transport.
symbols.core:
options: Optional collector policies; omitted options use message/peer stages, metadata-only capture and bounded default capacities.
Caller-owned IRpcDevtools, also IRpcProbe from @migaia/rpc-core/probe. Close explicitly; invalid construction options throw native TypeError with INVALID_OPTION and original cause.
methods: Exact method path filter supplied by the application; methodless control events remain observable.
No method filter; all method-bearing events are eligible.
sample: Deterministic sampling fraction in the interval greater than zero through one, using sender/message identity rather than random per-stage decisions.
`1`, retaining all eligible identities before retention limits.
capture: Explicit stages whose content may be read. Select names from RpcProbeStageName in @migaia/rpc-core/probe and keep capture within initially subscribed stages.
No content capture; observation remains metadata-only.
redact: Synchronous callback receiving numeric RpcProbeStage and captured content. Return the retained replacement; never retain the reusable event view. Collector executes it during ingestion, log executes it at the canonical emitter.
redact.stage: Numeric stage from RpcProbeStage supplied by the observing emitter.
redact.content: Captured caller-owned content reference from an explicitly enabled stage.
Replacement content, including undefined to discard it. Synchronous throws discard content and are reported; asynchronous redaction is not awaited.
No redactor; explicitly captured content retains its original reference.
Set it when explicitly captured content contains data that should not be retained or logged. Return a replacement, or `undefined` to discard content. Omitting it retains the captured reference unchanged; a thrown error is reported and that content is dropped.
onError: Synchronous observer receiving an original diagnostic error. Return nothing; observer failures are reported through the host failure channel without changing the RPC operation.
onError.error: Original collector, logger, formatter or observation failure supplied by the owning component.
No result is used and no asynchronous work is awaited by this callback boundary.
Uses the Core hostRethrowReporter failure channel; hub reporting instead defaults to console.error.
Set this callback when a diagnostic failure should reach the application monitor. It receives collector, formatter, logger or hub observer failures without replacing a business result. Omission keeps the documented host reporter for the owning component.
stages: Initial stage names from Core RpcProbeStageName; physical stages require explicit selection and selection alone never enables capture.
`["message", "peer"]`; physical stages are not subscribed.
Logical request, response and control observations.
Connection lifecycle observations.
Envelope observations; explicit opt-in.
Encoded content observations; explicit opt-in.
Frame observations; explicit opt-in.
Protected content observations; explicit opt-in.
Physical carrier observations; explicit opt-in.

maxEvents: Main-ring positive safe integer capacity, at most the JavaScript array length limit; newest events evict oldest events.
10000 retained events in the main ring.
maxContentBytes: Nonnegative safe integer budget for content retained by the main query ring; independent recording/watch references and opaque-object sizing are outside this byte total. It is not a process-wide memory ceiling; excess content drops while metadata stays.
8388608 bytes, or eight mebibytes.

65536 names; ingestion itself retains raw string references.
exposeContent: Allows captured content across the portable service boundary; local query and stopped recordings already use their retained captured content.
false; service responses omit captured content.

symbols.name: IRpcDevtools
symbols.purpose: Collector returned by createRpcDevtools, composed with external IRpcProbe. The Core owns stage masks and setStages; this collector owns retention, queries, recording, service projection and explicit close.
symbols.core:
emit: Consumes a Core-owned reusable IRpcProbeEventView synchronously into retained columns; never keeps the view itself. Installed emitters normally call it through probePlugin.
emit.view: IRpcProbeEventView issued by an installed Core emitter, valid only during its synchronous emit call; external type semantics remain in @migaia/rpc-core/probe.
Metadata is retained or accounted as filtered, paused, closed or reentrant loss. Observation failures are reported instead of reaching the business caller.
query: Synchronously scans retained events with compiled filters. This is a snapshot rather than a subscription; limits are one through one thousand.
query.input: Optional IRpcDevtoolsQuery; default cursor zero, limit one thousand and no field filters. Take subsequent afterSeq from the prior page nextSeq.
IRpcDevtoolsPage with events, nextSeq and loss counters. Invalid inputs use INVALID_OPTION and closed collectors use CLOSED.
watch: Subscribes from first generator advancement to future filtered events. Batches contain at most 256 events and each watcher retains at most 64 queued batches; overflow is counted rather than blocking RPC.
watch.input: Optional query filters excluding afterSeq and limit; defaults to no filters. Use query separately for retained history.
AsyncGenerator<IRpcDevtoolsWatchBatch>; return wakes a pending local next and releases the watcher without needing Collector.close. Collector close instead wakes pending reads with CLOSED; remote stream cancellation ends its service watcher normally.
stats: Snapshots endpoint/method settlement aggregates independently from query-ring eviction; clear resets them.
IRpcDevtoolsStats with cumulative counts and histogram-derived quantiles; a closed collector throws CLOSED.
describe: Reports the current monotonic clock sample, pause state, known endpoint descriptors, limits and loss counters.
IRpcDevtoolsDescribe snapshot; descriptors preserve their element references. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
record: Starts one independent bounded recording ring. Pair its handle stop() with exportRecord to obtain an offline record; only one recording may be active.
record.options: Optional maxEvents positive safe integer capacity, defaulting to the collector maxEvents. This bound is separate from main query retention.
A handle with stop(): IRpcDevtoolsRecord, taking no arguments and stopping only its own active ring. Duplicate start throws RECORD_ACTIVE; a stale or repeated stop throws RECORD_NOT_ACTIVE; closure throws CLOSED.
exportRecord: Encodes a stopped record through the standalone canonical record codec; this method does not change retained collector state.
exportRecord.record: IRpcDevtoolsRecord returned by a recording handle stop or record decoder.
Version-one NDJSON string; unsupported record input throws RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID with cause.
importRecord: Decodes offline text into an independent record; it does not append events to this collector or change its ring.
importRecord.text: Version-one text returned by exportRecord or encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord.
IRpcDevtoolsRecord with revived native errors and bytes, or RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID with cause.
pause: Snapshots current effective stage subscriptions and replaces them with an empty selection. Repeated pause is harmless; retained data remains queryable.
Collection is paused without pausing business RPC; closed collectors throw CLOSED.
resume: Restores the effective stage selection saved by the first pause. It does not revive a closed collector.
Collection resumes with prior subscriptions; repeated resume is harmless and closed collectors throw CLOSED.
clear: Clears main query retention, aggregate statistics and loss counters. Independent recording and watch windows keep their ownership.
Main retention and statistics are empty; the collector stays open. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
close: Idempotently removes subscriptions, releases retained storage and wakes pending watchers. It owns no serving Peer and does not close application endpoints.
Collector storage and subscriptions are released synchronously; later operational calls reject with CLOSED.
service: IRuntimePeerProvide object installed by the caller on a separate serving Peer, commonly under a devtools namespace. Service endpoints are excluded using actual localEndpointId; the caller owns transport and Peer lifetime.
symbols.advanced: Observe endpoint traffic locally and serve a separate diagnostics connection without owning business transports.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Collector returned by createRpcDevtools, composed with external IRpcProbe. The Core owns stage masks and setStages; this collector owns retention, queries, recording, service projection and explicit close.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import IRpcDevtools from @migaia/rpc-devtools, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use IRpcDevtools when its type contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when IRpcDevtools does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained type example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
emit: Consumes a Core-owned reusable IRpcProbeEventView synchronously into retained columns; never keeps the view itself. Installed emitters normally call it through probePlugin.
emit.view: IRpcProbeEventView issued by an installed Core emitter, valid only during its synchronous emit call; external type semantics remain in @migaia/rpc-core/probe.
Metadata is retained or accounted as filtered, paused, closed or reentrant loss. Observation failures are reported instead of reaching the business caller.
query: Synchronously scans retained events with compiled filters. This is a snapshot rather than a subscription; limits are one through one thousand.
query.input: Optional IRpcDevtoolsQuery; default cursor zero, limit one thousand and no field filters. Take subsequent afterSeq from the prior page nextSeq.
IRpcDevtoolsPage with events, nextSeq and loss counters. Invalid inputs use INVALID_OPTION and closed collectors use CLOSED.
watch: Subscribes from first generator advancement to future filtered events. Batches contain at most 256 events and each watcher retains at most 64 queued batches; overflow is counted rather than blocking RPC.
watch.input: Optional query filters excluding afterSeq and limit; defaults to no filters. Use query separately for retained history.
AsyncGenerator<IRpcDevtoolsWatchBatch>; return wakes a pending local next and releases the watcher without needing Collector.close. Collector close instead wakes pending reads with CLOSED; remote stream cancellation ends its service watcher normally.
stats: Snapshots endpoint/method settlement aggregates independently from query-ring eviction; clear resets them.
IRpcDevtoolsStats with cumulative counts and histogram-derived quantiles; a closed collector throws CLOSED.
describe: Reports the current monotonic clock sample, pause state, known endpoint descriptors, limits and loss counters.
IRpcDevtoolsDescribe snapshot; descriptors preserve their element references. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
record: Starts one independent bounded recording ring. Pair its handle stop() with exportRecord to obtain an offline record; only one recording may be active.
record.options: Optional maxEvents positive safe integer capacity, defaulting to the collector maxEvents. This bound is separate from main query retention.
A handle with stop(): IRpcDevtoolsRecord, taking no arguments and stopping only its own active ring. Duplicate start throws RECORD_ACTIVE; a stale or repeated stop throws RECORD_NOT_ACTIVE; closure throws CLOSED.
exportRecord: Encodes a stopped record through the standalone canonical record codec; this method does not change retained collector state.
exportRecord.record: IRpcDevtoolsRecord returned by a recording handle stop or record decoder.
Version-one NDJSON string; unsupported record input throws RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID with cause.
importRecord: Decodes offline text into an independent record; it does not append events to this collector or change its ring.
importRecord.text: Version-one text returned by exportRecord or encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord.
IRpcDevtoolsRecord with revived native errors and bytes, or RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID with cause.
pause: Snapshots current effective stage subscriptions and replaces them with an empty selection. Repeated pause is harmless; retained data remains queryable.
Collection is paused without pausing business RPC; closed collectors throw CLOSED.
resume: Restores the effective stage selection saved by the first pause. It does not revive a closed collector.
Collection resumes with prior subscriptions; repeated resume is harmless and closed collectors throw CLOSED.
clear: Clears main query retention, aggregate statistics and loss counters. Independent recording and watch windows keep their ownership.
Main retention and statistics are empty; the collector stays open. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
close: Idempotently removes subscriptions, releases retained storage and wakes pending watchers. It owns no serving Peer and does not close application endpoints.
Collector storage and subscriptions are released synchronously; later operational calls reject with CLOSED.
service: IRuntimePeerProvide object installed by the caller on a separate serving Peer, commonly under a devtools namespace. Service endpoints are excluded using actual localEndpointId; the caller owns transport and Peer lifetime.

symbols.name: IRpcDevtoolsOptions
symbols.purpose: Construction policies for a bounded collector; capacities are captured once, while effective subscriptions can later change through the Core probe setStages API.
symbols.core:
methods: Exact method path filter supplied by the application; methodless control events remain observable.
No method filter; all method-bearing events are eligible.
sample: Deterministic sampling fraction in the interval greater than zero through one, using sender/message identity rather than random per-stage decisions.
`1`, retaining all eligible identities before retention limits.
capture: Explicit stages whose content may be read. Select names from RpcProbeStageName in @migaia/rpc-core/probe and keep capture within initially subscribed stages.
No content capture; observation remains metadata-only.
redact: Synchronous callback receiving numeric RpcProbeStage and captured content. Return the retained replacement; never retain the reusable event view. Collector executes it during ingestion, log executes it at the canonical emitter.
redact.stage: Numeric stage from RpcProbeStage supplied by the observing emitter.
redact.content: Captured caller-owned content reference from an explicitly enabled stage.
Replacement content, including undefined to discard it. Synchronous throws discard content and are reported; asynchronous redaction is not awaited.
No redactor; explicitly captured content retains its original reference.
Set it when explicitly captured content contains data that should not be retained or logged. Return a replacement, or `undefined` to discard content. Omitting it retains the captured reference unchanged; a thrown error is reported and that content is dropped.
onError: Synchronous observer receiving an original diagnostic error. Return nothing; observer failures are reported through the host failure channel without changing the RPC operation.
onError.error: Original collector, logger, formatter or observation failure supplied by the owning component.
No result is used and no asynchronous work is awaited by this callback boundary.
Uses the Core hostRethrowReporter failure channel; hub reporting instead defaults to console.error.
Set this callback when a diagnostic failure should reach the application monitor. It receives collector, formatter, logger or hub observer failures without replacing a business result. Omission keeps the documented host reporter for the owning component.
stages: Initial stage names from Core RpcProbeStageName; physical stages require explicit selection and selection alone never enables capture.
`["message", "peer"]`; physical stages are not subscribed.
Logical request, response and control observations.
Connection lifecycle observations.
Envelope observations; explicit opt-in.
Encoded content observations; explicit opt-in.
Frame observations; explicit opt-in.
Protected content observations; explicit opt-in.
Physical carrier observations; explicit opt-in.
Use `message` for logical calls and `peer` for connection lifecycle. Add `envelope`, `encoded`, `frame`, `protected` or `carrier` to inspect those physical processing steps. Omission selects message and peer; choosing a stage never enables content capture by itself.
maxEvents: Main-ring positive safe integer capacity, at most the JavaScript array length limit; newest events evict oldest events.
10000 retained events in the main ring.
maxContentBytes: Nonnegative safe integer budget for content retained by the main query ring; independent recording/watch references and opaque-object sizing are outside this byte total. It is not a process-wide memory ceiling; excess content drops while metadata stays.
8388608 bytes, or eight mebibytes.
maxInterned: Positive safe integer reader name-table bound, at most floor(sqrt(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)) minus one; overflow uses an explicit marker.
65536 names; ingestion itself retains raw string references.
exposeContent: Allows captured content across the portable service boundary; local query and stopped recordings already use their retained captured content.
false; service responses omit captured content.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

guidance.id: 往返保存捕获字节与原生错误链
guidance.heading: 往返保存捕获字节与原生错误链

blocks.text: 离线诊断文件既要保存字节载荷，也要保留失败操作背后的原始原因。
直接使用普通 JSON 会把类型化字节变成对象字段，并丢掉 Error 的不可枚举属性，导入后的事故信息因此不完整。
把完整 v1 记录交给 `encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord`，再用配套解码器读取，编解码器负责保留字节标签与原生错误图。
输出：

blocks.code:
true true
true
1,2,3

blocks.text: 输出 `true true`、`true`、`1,2,3`：解码还原 Error 及其 TypeError 原因，保留记录中的堆栈，并还原字节值。
编解码器只转换离线表示，不执行文件读写；单键 `$bytes` 对象属于 v1 保留语法，不保证任意对象、原型和函数都能无损往返。

symbols.name: encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord
symbols.signature: export declare function encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord(record: IRpcDevtoolsRecord): string;
symbols.purpose: Encodes ordered record events as version-one NDJSON with a header line and trailing newline. Bytes use canonical padded Base64 tags; native errors delegate to the canonical Contract error graph and retain stacks.
symbols.core:
record: IRpcDevtoolsRecord from a stopped recording or an application-built record using RpcDevtoolsRecordFormat.
Complete NDJSON string; unsupported header, event, bytes or error conversion throws RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID with original cause. Input errors and stacks are not mutated.
parameters: record: IRpcDevtoolsRecord
symbols.returns: string
examples:
import { createRpcDevtoolsHub } from '@migaia/rpc-devtools/hub'
import * as format from '@migaia/rpc-devtools/contract'

const outbound = {
  seq: 1,
  at: 10,
  endpointId: 'client',
  stage: 'message',
  direction: 'outbound',
  kind: 'request',
  senderId: 'client',
  messageId: 'call-1',
  method: 'load',
  trace: 'trace-1'
}
const inbound = { ...outbound, at: 11, endpointId: 'server', direction: 'inbound' }
const encode = (event: typeof outbound) =>
  format.encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord({ header: format.RpcDevtoolsRecordFormat, events: [event] })
const hub = createRpcDevtoolsHub()
try {
  hub.importRecord('caller', encode(outbound))
  console.log(hub.interactions('trace-1')[0]?.oneSided)
  hub.importRecord('provider', encode(inbound))
  const interaction = hub.interactions('trace-1')[0]
  console.log(interaction?.oneSided, interaction?.targets.join(','))
  await hub.removeTarget('provider')
  await hub.removeTarget('provider')
  console.log(hub.status('provider'), hub.interactions('trace-1')[0]?.oneSided)
} finally {
  await hub.close()
}

symbols.name: IRpcDevtoolsRecordEvent
symbols.purpose: Wire event fields with an error override accepting a native Error or the external canonical wire error graph. Decoding restores native errors without rebuilding their stacks.
symbols.core:
target: Optional hub-supplied target name from addTarget or importRecord, separate from Core endpoint identity.
Absent in ordinary collector events without a hub target projection.
seq: Collector-domain sequence issued during ingestion; use query nextSeq for pagination rather than physical ring offsets.
carrierSeq: Collector-domain sequence pointing to an observed inbound carrier origin in this target; absence means no retained resolved link.
Absent when no originating carrier link can be resolved.
at: Timestamp supplied by the observing Core emitter; hub alignment wraps it without modifying this original number.
endpointId: Endpoint identifier issued by the Core endpoint constructor and captured by its emitter.
stage: Canonical stage name from RpcProbeStageName in the Core probe contract.
direction: Canonical inbound or outbound direction name from the Core probe contract.
kind: Optional logical message kind name from the Core probe taxonomy; physical-only observations may omit it.
Absent when the observing layer cannot identify a logical message kind.
outcome: Optional canonical event outcome name used by queries and settlement statistics.
Absent when the observation has no outcome classification.
messageId: Message identifier issued by the originating RPC sender; combine with senderId for interaction correlation.
Absent when no logical message identity is observable.
method: Method path observed on the logical message; names originate from the caller method route.
Absent on observations without a logical method route.
variation: Original variation route observed on message or envelope stages, preserving the Core route vocabulary.
Absent on stages where no variation route is observed.
senderId: Originating sender identity supplied by the observed RPC message.
Absent when the observed layer has no sender identity.
targetId: Destination identity supplied by the observed RPC routing envelope.
Absent when no destination identity is available.
receiverId: Actual receiver identity supplied by the observed receive path, which may differ from a routing target.
Absent when the receive layer cannot expose a receiver.
peerId: Peer identity issued by the observed Core peer lifecycle path.
Absent when the event is unrelated to an identified peer.
trace: Explicit application-provided trace carried by the observed message; native Peer calls do not automatically invent it.
Absent unless the application propagates a trace.
sizeBytes: Observed byte count when the layer knows it; missing sizes are not substituted with zero.
Absent when the source reports its unknown-size sentinel.
chunk: Observed chunk position: index is the source chunk index and count is its source chunk count; values come from the Core event.
Absent when the event is not an observed chunk.
members: Observed batch member count supplied by the source event.
Absent when the event has no batch member count.
durationMs: Observed settlement duration in milliseconds; aggregates accept nonnegative durations on message settlement outcomes.
Absent when the source event does not describe settlement.
rejection: Package-local rejection reason from the observed provider boundary, distinguishing causes that share an error code.
Absent when no rejection reason is observed.
lifecycle: Observed Core lifecycle event name, retaining the emitting owner vocabulary.
Absent outside lifecycle observations.
error: Optional native Error or IRpcWireError supplied by a stopped recording or application; codec preserves the canonical cause graph and stacks.
Absent when no error belongs to the event.
carrier: Observed physical carrier name supplied by the adapter or Core descriptor.
Absent when the source cannot identify a physical carrier.
detail: Adapter-owned scalar detail record; keys describe the observed carrier, and retained values are not deeply copied.
Absent when the observing carrier exposes no detail record.
content: Opted-in captured reference after redaction; mutating or transferring its backing may affect later reads. Service exposure separately requires exposeContent. The record codec reserves any nested single-key {$bytes: base64} object for byte revival; use JSON text for a same-shaped business object.
Absent in metadata-only mode or after redaction/budget removal.

at: Timestamp supplied by the observing Core emitter; hub alignment wraps it without modifying this original number.
endpointId: Endpoint identifier issued by the Core endpoint constructor and captured by its emitter.
stage: Canonical stage name from RpcProbeStageName in the Core probe contract.
direction: Canonical inbound or outbound direction name from the Core probe contract.
kind: Optional logical message kind name from the Core probe taxonomy; physical-only observations may omit it.
Absent when the observing layer cannot identify a logical message kind.
outcome: Optional canonical event outcome name used by queries and settlement statistics.
Absent when the observation has no outcome classification.
messageId: Message identifier issued by the originating RPC sender; combine with senderId for interaction correlation.
Absent when no logical message identity is observable.
method: Method path observed on the logical message; names originate from the caller method route.
Absent on observations without a logical method route.
variation: Original variation route observed on message or envelope stages, preserving the Core route vocabulary.
Absent on stages where no variation route is observed.
senderId: Originating sender identity supplied by the observed RPC message.
Absent when the observed layer has no sender identity.
targetId: Destination identity supplied by the observed RPC routing envelope.
Absent when no destination identity is available.
receiverId: Actual receiver identity supplied by the observed receive path, which may differ from a routing target.
Absent when the receive layer cannot expose a receiver.
peerId: Peer identity issued by the observed Core peer lifecycle path.
Absent when the event is unrelated to an identified peer.
trace: Explicit application-provided trace carried by the observed message; native Peer calls do not automatically invent it.
Absent unless the application propagates a trace.
sizeBytes: Observed byte count when the layer knows it; missing sizes are not substituted with zero.
Absent when the source reports its unknown-size sentinel.
chunk: Observed chunk position: index is the source chunk index and count is its source chunk count; values come from the Core event.
Absent when the event is not an observed chunk.
members: Observed batch member count supplied by the source event.
Absent when the event has no batch member count.
durationMs: Observed settlement duration in milliseconds; aggregates accept nonnegative durations on message settlement outcomes.
Absent when the source event does not describe settlement.
rejection: Package-local rejection reason from the observed provider boundary, distinguishing causes that share an error code.
Absent when no rejection reason is observed.
lifecycle: Observed Core lifecycle event name, retaining the emitting owner vocabulary.
Absent outside lifecycle observations.
error: Canonical serialized error graph owned by @migaia/rpc-contract/errors, retaining source, code, stack and causes.
Absent when no error is attached to the observation.
carrier: Observed physical carrier name supplied by the adapter or Core descriptor.
Absent when the source cannot identify a physical carrier.
detail: Adapter-owned scalar detail record; keys describe the observed carrier, and retained values are not deeply copied.
Absent when the observing carrier exposes no detail record.
content: Opted-in captured reference after redaction; mutating or transferring its backing may affect later reads. Service exposure separately requires exposeContent. The record codec reserves any nested single-key {$bytes: base64} object for byte revival; use JSON text for a same-shaped business object.
Absent in metadata-only mode or after redaction/budget removal.

symbols.name: RpcDevtoolsRecordFormat
symbols.purpose: Frozen version-one record header identity containing format migaia-rpc-devtools and version one. Use the same object when constructing records for the codec; it carries no clock or descriptor metadata.
symbols.core:
format: migaia-rpc-devtools selects this package offline record grammar.
version: One selects the frozen first record grammar; unsupported versions reject.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this const.
examples:
import { createRpcDevtoolsHub } from '@migaia/rpc-devtools/hub'
import * as format from '@migaia/rpc-devtools/contract'

const outbound = {
  seq: 1,
  at: 10,
  endpointId: 'client',
  stage: 'message',
  direction: 'outbound',
  kind: 'request',
  senderId: 'client',
  messageId: 'call-1',
  method: 'load',
  trace: 'trace-1'
}
const inbound = { ...outbound, at: 11, endpointId: 'server', direction: 'inbound' }
const encode = (event: typeof outbound) =>
  format.encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord({ header: format.RpcDevtoolsRecordFormat, events: [event] })
const hub = createRpcDevtoolsHub()
try {
  hub.importRecord('caller', encode(outbound))
  console.log(hub.interactions('trace-1')[0]?.oneSided)
  hub.importRecord('provider', encode(inbound))
  const interaction = hub.interactions('trace-1')[0]
  console.log(interaction?.oneSided, interaction?.targets.join(','))
  await hub.removeTarget('provider')
  await hub.removeTarget('provider')
  console.log(hub.status('provider'), hub.interactions('trace-1')[0]?.oneSided)
} finally {
  await hub.close()
}

guidance.id: 往返保存捕获字节与原生错误链
guidance.heading: 往返保存捕获字节与原生错误链

blocks.text: 离线诊断文件既要保存字节载荷，也要保留失败操作背后的原始原因。
直接使用普通 JSON 会把类型化字节变成对象字段，并丢掉 Error 的不可枚举属性，导入后的事故信息因此不完整。
把完整 v1 记录交给 `encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord`，再用配套解码器读取，编解码器负责保留字节标签与原生错误图。
输出：

blocks.code:
true true
true
1,2,3

blocks.text: 输出 `true true`、`true`、`1,2,3`：解码还原 Error 及其 TypeError 原因，保留记录中的堆栈，并还原字节值。
编解码器只转换离线表示，不执行文件读写；单键 `$bytes` 对象属于 v1 保留语法，不保证任意对象、原型和函数都能无损往返。

symbols.name: createRpcDevtoolsHub
symbols.purpose: Creates a caller-owned multi-target observation hub. Live registration samples describe five times, chooses minimum round-trip alignment, starts the first read of one watch before querying retained pages, then consumes that bounded watch and deduplicates by sequence. Offline import uses no invented clock metadata; existing clients remain caller-owned.
symbols.core:
options: Optional per-target retention, realignment period and error observer. Omitted settings retain fifty thousand events per target without periodic realignment.
IRpcDevtoolsHub; close returns the same promise on repeated calls. Invalid options throw INVALID_OPTION; target and lifecycle errors use the package error table.
maxEvents: Positive safe per-target retention capacity, at most 4294967295 events.
50000 events independently for each target.
realignMs: Finite positive period in milliseconds for five-sample live target realignment; at most one realignment runs per target.
`undefined`; only initial live registration performs alignment.
onError: Synchronous observer receiving an original diagnostic error. Return nothing; observer failures are reported through the host failure channel without changing the RPC operation.
onError.error: Original collector, logger, formatter or observation failure supplied by the owning component.
No result is used and no asynchronous work is awaited by this callback boundary.
Reports failures with host console.error; a supplied callback that throws is reported with the original error in an aggregate.
Set this callback when a diagnostic failure should reach the application monitor. It receives collector, formatter, logger or hub observer failures without replacing a business result. Omission keeps the documented host reporter for the owning component.
parameters: options: IRpcDevtoolsHubOptions (optional)
symbols.returns: IRpcDevtoolsHub

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
target: Application name registered through addTarget or importRecord.
alignedAt: Original event timestamp minus target offset; offline records use offset zero.
uncertaintyMs: Half the minimum round-trip duration among five alignment samples; undefined for offline records without clock metadata.
interaction: Hub-issued correlation key derived from observed sender/message identity or a resolved carrier link.

trace: Explicit trace copied from the original event or its observed logical correlation.

event: Original IRpcDevtoolsWireEvent reference retained without changing its source timestamp.

symbols.name: createRpcLogProbe
symbols.purpose: Creates a standalone Core probe that logs qualifying failed, rejected, slow or peer-lifecycle events. Install it through probePlugin. Each qualifying event makes one synchronous logger call; sink promise rejection is observed without awaiting or changing business RPC.
symbols.core:
logger: Caller-owned IRpcLogSink with debug, info, warn and error methods, for example a compatible logger instance; it owns buffering and output.
options: Optional logging policy; default stages are message and peer, content capture and slow-call qualification are disabled.
IRpcProbe from @migaia/rpc-core/probe; its protocol surface remains owned there. Invalid sink or options throw TypeError with INVALID_OPTION, while observer failures use onError.
methods: Exact method path filter supplied by the application; methodless control events remain observable.
No method filter; all method-bearing events are eligible.
sample: Deterministic sampling fraction in the interval greater than zero through one, using sender/message identity rather than random per-stage decisions.
`1`, retaining all eligible identities before retention limits.
capture: Explicit stages whose content may be read. Select names from RpcProbeStageName in @migaia/rpc-core/probe and keep capture within initially subscribed stages.
No content capture; observation remains metadata-only.
redact: Synchronous callback receiving numeric RpcProbeStage and captured content. Return the retained replacement; never retain the reusable event view. Collector executes it during ingestion, log executes it at the canonical emitter.
redact.stage: Numeric stage from RpcProbeStage supplied by the observing emitter.
redact.content: Captured caller-owned content reference from an explicitly enabled stage.
Replacement content, including undefined to discard it. Synchronous throws discard content and are reported; asynchronous redaction is not awaited.
No redactor; explicitly captured content retains its original reference.
Set it when explicitly captured content contains data that should not be retained or logged. Return a replacement, or `undefined` to discard content. Omitting it retains the captured reference unchanged; a thrown error is reported and that content is dropped.
onError: Synchronous observer receiving an original diagnostic error. Return nothing; observer failures are reported through the host failure channel without changing the RPC operation.
onError.error: Original collector, logger, formatter or observation failure supplied by the owning component.
No result is used and no asynchronous work is awaited by this callback boundary.
Uses the Core hostRethrowReporter failure channel; hub reporting instead defaults to console.error.
Set this callback when a diagnostic failure should reach the application monitor. It receives collector, formatter, logger or hub observer failures without replacing a business result. Omission keeps the documented host reporter for the owning component.
slowMs: Finite nonnegative settlement duration threshold for successful slow-call logging.
`undefined`; successful calls do not qualify as slow.
stages: Subscribed log stages; only message settlements and peer lifecycle belong to this helper.
message and peer stages.
Observe message settlement failures, rejections and configured slow calls.
Observe peer lifecycle events using the lifecycle log category.
Select `message` for failed, rejected or slow calls, and `peer` for connection lifecycle. Omission selects both. This log helper accepts no physical stages; selecting stages alone does not enable content capture.
content: Enables capture for subscribed stages when capture is omitted; explicit capture also permits captured fields to reach the logger.
false, with capture disabled unless explicitly requested.
levels: Category overrides: failed, rejected, timeout, aborted, slow and lifecycle map to a named sink level or off.
failed uses error, lifecycle uses info, and rejected/timeout/aborted/slow use warn.
Invoke logger.debug once for a qualifying event of the selected category.
Invoke logger.info once; default for peer lifecycle observations.
Invoke logger.warn once; default for rejection, timeout, abort and slow events.
Invoke logger.error once; default for ordinary call failures.
Skip message construction and logger invocation for this category.
Override individual categories when their default severity does not fit the application. `debug`, `info`, `warn` and `error` choose the corresponding logger method; `off` skips that category. Omitted categories retain their documented defaults.
message: Synchronous formatter called only for qualifying enabled events. Receives a reusable Core event view valid during the callback; return a string and never retain the view. Throws are reported through onError.
message.view: Emitter-owned IRpcProbeEventView supplied for one synchronous formatting call.
String passed as logger message; async formatters are unsupported.
Stable built-in message for the classified failure, rejection, timeout, abort, slow or lifecycle category.
Set a formatter when the logger needs application-specific text. Return a string synchronously and read the view only during the callback. Omitting it uses the built-in category message; a thrown error is reported through `onError`.
Install the returned IRpcProbe through Core probePlugin. Existing endpoint observation gains qualified logger dispatch; no request methods or transport ownership are added.

symbols.purpose: The application logger supplied to the log probe, with required debug, info, warn and error methods. The probe forwards matching RPC events to these methods. Each method runs with the original logger as its receiver, so it can use that logger's instance state. A thrown error or rejection is passed to onError.

symbols.name: createProcessPool
symbols.purpose: Creates independent Process Peers and applies pool-owned client-slot scheduling. Every member receives the original spawn source and probe; native Process runtime, wire format, permissions and restart budget remain unchanged. The spawned program uses createProcessPeer to provide its methods.
symbols.core:
Promise<IProcessPool<TRemote>> preserving Process public call-option types, including no native transfer lists. Invalid pool input uses INVALID_OPTIONS and original acquisition errors pass through; caller owns explicit pool close.
size: Required positive integer target count selected by the caller. Initial construction acquires that many independent public Peers before exposing the pool.
maxQueue: Nonnegative integer bound on FIFO waiters, excluding operations already assigned to members. Zero rejects immediately when every slot is busy.
256 waiting operations; overflow rejects QUEUE_FULL without calling a Peer.
idleTimeoutMs: Finite positive idle duration no greater than 2147483647 milliseconds. Retires genuinely idle members through their original close; future demand recreates missing target capacity.
undefined, disabling pool-owned idle retirement; native Peer supervision remains unchanged.
scheduler: IScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler or a compatible injected scheduler, controlling only pool idle timers and their optional unref.
systemScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler; Peer restart and deadline policy stays with each original spawn source.
spawn: Required NonNullable<IRuntimeProcessPeerOptions[spawn]> from @migaia/rpc-process: true for the guarded current entry, path, URL or original process source configuration. The program provides methods through createProcessPeer and the pool forwards the exact source unchanged.
probe: One IRpcProbe or readonly probe array from @migaia/rpc-core/probe, for example from createRpcDevtools. The exact same handle is forwarded to every public member factory; use event endpointId to distinguish members.
undefined; no pool-added source probe is passed to member factories.

declaredConfiguration.description: Maximum waiting FIFO length, default 256; nonnegative integer, with 0 allowing no queue.

rows: 必填且不能为 null / undefined；原值交给对应公开 Peer 工厂。
必填正整数；这是目标成员数，不是 provider 并发数。
256，非负整数；0 表示所有槽忙时不允许等待。
undefined，不做闲置回收；配置时为有限正数且不大于 2147483647 毫秒，允许小数。
undefined；接受原 Peer 的单个 Probe 或只读 Probe 数组，原值转交每个成员。

blocks.text: 非法 options 结构、缺少 spawn 或不正确的数值类型以 TypeError / INVALID_OPTIONS 拒绝；数值超出 size、maxQueue、idleTimeoutMs 的范围以 RangeError / INVALID_OPTIONS 拒绝，发生在原生工厂取得资源之前。这里没有额外的 safe-integer 要求，也没有 size 的自动默认值。scheduler 通过 lifecycle 的既有入口在原生工厂调用前捕获和校验，失败保留该 owner 的 source / code 与原因，不改成池错误；不要把这一点扩大为所有 options 字段的一次性深快照。

Thread 的 spawn 保留原工厂支持的 true、入口路径 / URL 与 source 配置；Process 同样保留其入口、运行时、权限和 wire 规则。不同程序可以用不同入口；Process 的外语 JSON-RPC source 仍使用原 `{ command, args, wire: 'jsonrpc', contract }`。这些 source 的字段属于相应工厂，不是池新定义的启动协议。

`spawn: true` 会重新执行主入口，必须先用原 `await isThreadChild()` 或 `isProcessChild()` 区分子端，避免再次建池。相对字符串按主入口目录解释，URL 精确定位入口；浏览器线程沿原 URL 规则。Node 的 TypeScript 去类型不会把源码中的 .js 导入改写为 .ts，需使用可运行的编译输出或适当 loader。只通过主机权限、入口和 native lifetime 约束允许的原生路径启动。

blocks.text: `createThreadPool<TRemote>(options)` 和 `createProcessPool<TRemote>(options)` 异步返回池，初始成员批次全部取得后才交给调用方。远端类型默认 `Record<never, never>`，由应用声明业务方法；该泛型不是运行时 schema 或远端方法安装。

rows: 必填且不能为 null / undefined；原值交给对应公开 Peer 工厂。
必填正整数；这是目标成员数，不是 provider 并发数。
256，非负整数；0 表示所有槽忙时不允许等待。
undefined，不做闲置回收；配置时为有限正数且不大于 2147483647 毫秒，允许小数。
undefined；接受原 Peer 的单个 Probe 或只读 Probe 数组，原值转交每个成员。

blocks.text: 非法 options 结构、缺少 spawn 或不正确的数值类型以 TypeError / INVALID_OPTIONS 拒绝；数值超出 size、maxQueue、idleTimeoutMs 的范围以 RangeError / INVALID_OPTIONS 拒绝，发生在原生工厂取得资源之前。这里没有额外的 safe-integer 要求，也没有 size 的自动默认值。scheduler 通过 lifecycle 的既有入口在原生工厂调用前捕获和校验，失败保留该 owner 的 source / code 与原因，不改成池错误；不要把这一点扩大为所有 options 字段的一次性深快照。

Thread 的 spawn 保留原工厂支持的 true、入口路径 / URL 与 source 配置；Process 同样保留其入口、运行时、权限和 wire 规则。不同程序可以用不同入口；Process 的外语 JSON-RPC source 仍使用原 `{ command, args, wire: 'jsonrpc', contract }`。这些 source 的字段属于相应工厂，不是池新定义的启动协议。

`spawn: true` 会重新执行主入口，必须先用原 `await isThreadChild()` 或 `isProcessChild()` 区分子端，避免再次建池。相对字符串按主入口目录解释，URL 精确定位入口；浏览器线程沿原 URL 规则。Node 的 TypeScript 去类型不会把源码中的 .js 导入改写为 .ts，需使用可运行的编译输出或适当 loader。只通过主机权限、入口和 native lifetime 约束允许的原生路径启动。

symbols.name: IProcessPool
symbols.signature:
export type IProcessPool<TRemote = Record<never, never>> = Pick<
  Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createProcessPeer<TRemote>>>,
  'request' | 'notify' | 'stream'
> &
  IRpcPoolControls;
symbols.purpose: Caller-owned pool returned by createProcessPool. Preserves Process request, notify and stream types with no native transfer list, adding the same pool-owned lifecycle controls as Thread pools.
symbols.core:
request: Schedules one original Process Peer request. Queue waiting does not start the native deadline; the occupied slot is released only when the original result promise settles. Pool scheduling never retries a failed business call.
request.method: Dotted method path declared by the spawned Process provide API and checked against TRemote.
request.args: Original payload and Process call options from the application, including signal, timeoutMs and idempotencyKey. Process public types prohibit native transfer lists; the pool preserves that prohibition.
Promise of the original typed result after queued dispatch. Pool-owned admission may reject POOL_CLOSED, QUEUE_FULL or queued CALL_ABORTED; native and Peer errors keep original identity and source/code.
notify: Schedules one original Process Peer notification and holds its client slot until the send promise settles; no business response is awaited.
notify.method: One-way method route supplied by the spawned Process provide API.
notify.args: Original application payload and Process options, retaining caller cancellation and the prohibition on native transfer lists.
Promise<void> from the original send boundary after pool scheduling; pool queue failures use its own codes and original send failures pass through.
stream: Creates a lazy Process stream iterator, admitting work only at first next(). The slot remains owned until the original stream finishes or termination is forwarded; never starting it does not block pool close.
stream.method: Iterator method path provided by the spawned Process program and checked against TRemote.
stream.args: Original payload and Process stream options from the application, including signal; native transfer lists remain unsupported.
Original typed async iterator semantics behind pool admission. next() yields or rejects unchanged; return(value) and throw(error) forward original termination when available and release the slot exactly once.
stats: Returns the current pool client-slot and FIFO snapshot, including during or after close. This does not measure provider concurrency or native worker load.
Frozen IRpcPoolStats with target size, acquired member count, actual dispatched in-flight slots, queued waiters and pool state.
resize: Serializes target-size changes in call order. Expansion acquires a transactional batch; shrink retires idle members first and waits for busy retired members to finish their accepted operations.
resize.size: New positive integer target selected by the caller; it replaces the construction target after this resize is admitted.
Promise<void> after acquisition or retirement. Invalid size uses INVALID_OPTIONS; closure uses POOL_CLOSED. Expansion failure restores the previous target and retains the original factory failure.
Change capacity on an existing pool. This complete Node 24 example uses a guarded Thread entry with spawn true and required size 1; maxQueue defaults to 256, idleTimeoutMs to undefined and scheduler to systemScheduler. Each resize argument is the new required positive integer target.
close: Stops new admission, drains accepted queue entries and operations, then closes every owned member once. Long streams must end, return, throw or be cancelled to release their slot before drain can finish.
The same Promise<void> on repeated calls. Resolves after all member closes, or rejects with CLOSE_FAILED AggregateError retaining every original close failure and the first cause.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
size: Required positive integer target count selected by the caller. Initial construction acquires that many independent public Peers before exposing the pool.
maxQueue: Nonnegative integer bound on FIFO waiters, excluding operations already assigned to members. Zero rejects immediately when every slot is busy.
256 waiting operations; overflow rejects QUEUE_FULL without calling a Peer.
idleTimeoutMs: Finite positive idle duration no greater than 2147483647 milliseconds. Retires genuinely idle members through their original close; future demand recreates missing target capacity.
undefined, disabling pool-owned idle retirement; native Peer supervision remains unchanged.
scheduler: IScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler or a compatible injected scheduler, controlling only pool idle timers and their optional unref.
systemScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler; Peer restart and deadline policy stays with each original spawn source.
spawn: Required NonNullable<IRuntimeThreadPeerOptions[spawn]> from @migaia/rpc-threads: true for the guarded current entry, path, URL or original Thread spawn configuration. The spawned entry provides methods through createThreadPeer; every member receives this exact source.
probe: One IRpcProbe or readonly probe array from @migaia/rpc-core/probe, for example from createRpcDevtools. The exact same handle is forwarded to every public member factory; use event endpointId to distinguish members.
undefined; no pool-added source probe is passed to member factories.

短进程 source 可能经原 reporter 报告 supervision 的 CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED 提示，指出 process termination 不受支持并按 best-effort 降级；这不阻止已成功建立的业务调用，也不承诺整棵进程树的强制终止。池保留该原 owner 的诊断，不隐藏提示或增加另一套终止策略。

symbols.purpose: Advanced: `createProcessPlugin` with a custom runtime I/O loader.
symbols.core:
options: Either complete IProcessPluginOptions with deployment, or symmetric IRuntimeProcessPluginOptions with spawn/connect/listen and provide/expose.
runtime: Loader whose `load()` returns `{ processRuntimeIO }`.
Full deployment returns IProcessPlugin, including its deployment controls; symmetric source returns the Core runtime plugin for the process slot and does not promise replace.
name: Caller-selected nonempty registration name copied when constructing the cold plugin; use the same name when addressing host.process.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
contract: Application remote contract. Required and matched to name for a full deployment; optional for runtime sources, where provide normally supplies the directory.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
registrationOwner: Identifies the plugin registration that may be removed if its process cannot recover. In the full deployment form, supply the exact registration name and the Host that installs it. When failure reports remain unhandled, cleanup uses this Host to remove that registration. The name must equal options.name and the Host must provide unUse; missing or mismatched values reject configuration before process setup.
resilience: Caller-owned governance from createProcessResilience, borrowed by this plugin rather than closed with it.
Omitted: create and own a governor using the deployment scheduler and report callback.
host: Full deployment: Host port owning installation and replacement. Runtime form: the actual installing Host, needed only when exposing host control with catalog and resolvePlugin.
Omitted: allowed unless expose contains host; explicit host exposure requires host, catalog and resolvePlugin together.
endpointFactory: Endpoint factory called with the acquired channel and abort signal; mandatory for full deployments, while runtime sources can use canonical endpoint assembly.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Required in the full deployment overload; no endpoint factory is inferred.
Build the explicit full-deployment endpoint from this acquired channel; retain its pipeline and flow-control features.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
`defaultRpcReporter`, which reports through the default console path.
Route native process and background diagnostics to the application sink without printing credentials.
keyFactory: Key callback for automatically keyed idempotent calls in full deployments and managed runtime spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core assembly and do not consume it.
Application-issued string key for that call.
Omitted: the proxy uses defaultRpcId.
Managed process spawn/connect consumes this policy for declared idempotent requests. A function source uses direct Core assembly and does not consume this proxy policy.
retryPort: Whole-invocation dispatch port for full deployments and managed runtime spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use the direct Core call path.
Omitted: createRemoteRetryPort uses the binding events, scheduler and reporter.
deployment: Spawn or connect deployment.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
spawn: Child to start and own: `URL`, path (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (current entry), a short object `{ entry | command, args?, wrap?, wire?, ... }`, or a full `ISpawnProcessPluginDeployment`.
Not set.
connect: Running service to dial: a name (`math-service`), `tcp://127.0.0.1:port`, a Unix path, or a full connect deployment.
listen: Address or name to accept sessions on; each session is its own connection.
token: Shared secret checked in the handshake; required for TCP, explicit socket paths and Windows pipes. Generate it per deployment and never log it.
Not set: named endpoints rely on OS user permissions.
verify: Listener side: `(auth, peer) => principalId` validating the client credential; throw to reject.
verify.auth: Portable credential from the incoming handshake, possibly undefined.
verify.peer: Handshake peer metadata supplied by the accepted transport.
Verified principal string or its Promise; throw or rejection refuses the candidate.
Not set: the `token` comparison is used.
Require an application principal for a listener rather than relying only on same-user socket permissions.
connectTimeoutMs: How long a named `connect` waits for the listener to appear.
`5000`.
expose: Distinct nonempty paths explicitly exposing current Host feature methods, runtime connection routes or the reserved host control entry. Only this snapshotted whitelist becomes remotely callable.
Omitted: an empty whitelist; only provide methods are published.
catalog: Application-authored IRemoteHostCatalog declaring the only plugin contracts available through explicitly exposed host control.
Omitted: no host-control catalog; required when expose contains host.
resolvePlugin: Synchronous local resolver invoked by the canonical host-control owner after catalog admission; definitions remain local and are installed through the original Host.
resolvePlugin.name: Plugin name admitted by the declared catalog.
resolvePlugin.config: Optional portable configuration from the remote host-use request.
Local plugin definition accepted by the Host; a thrown error rejects the host-use request.
Omitted: no local resolver; required when expose contains host.
Resolve only catalog-admitted names to local definitions when host is explicitly exposed.
registrationOwner.name: Names the one registration that failure cleanup may remove. Set it to the value of options.name for this plugin before constructing the full deployment. A different name rejects configuration, preventing failure handling for this plugin from removing another registration.
registrationOwner.host: Supplies the Host that actually installs this plugin. Failure cleanup invokes its unUse method to remove the named registration and apply the Host rules for dependent plugins. Pass that original Host; an object without unUse is rejected before process setup. The caller continues to own the Host.
