symbols.name: createProcessPeer
symbols.purpose: Opens a Runtime Peer to another process. Choose one source: `spawn` starts and owns a child, `connect` dials a running service, and `listen` binds an accepting endpoint. A library-launched child may omit the source to connect back. Spawn/connect/child discovery resolves after readiness; listen resolves after binding, before any client must arrive.
symbols.core:
options: See `IRuntimeProcessPeerOptions`: source, `provide`, `report` (default `defaultRpcReporter`), `token`, `verify`, `connectTimeoutMs`, `defaultTimeoutMs` (default `30000`) and Core Peer options.
An `IRuntimeTypedPeer<TRemote>`. `close()` stops new work and drains/closes under the owning runtime budget, normally `5000` ms narrowed by remaining stop time; it does not guarantee uncooperative calls finish. Spawn ownership also stops its child.
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
Keep an existing endpoint composition for the acquired process channel; use its actual codec, framer and flow-control features.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
`defaultRpcReporter`, which reports through the default console path.
Route native process and background diagnostics to the application sink without printing credentials.
keyFactory: Application key generator for automatically keyed idempotent requests on managed spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core Peer assembly and do not consume this proxy field.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
Managed process spawn/connect consumes this policy for declared idempotent requests. A function source uses direct Core assembly and does not consume this proxy policy.
retryPort: Whole-invocation dispatch port for managed spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core Peer assembly and do not consume this field.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
spawn: Child to start and own: `URL`, path (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (current entry), a short object `{ entry | command, args?, wrap?, wire?, ... }`, or a full `ISpawnProcessPluginDeployment`.
Not set.
connect: Running service to dial: a name (`math-service`), `tcp://127.0.0.1:port`, a Unix path, or a full connect deployment.
listen: Address or name to accept sessions on; each session is its own connection.
token: Shared secret checked in the handshake; required for TCP, explicit socket paths and Windows pipes. Generate it per deployment and never log it.
Not set: named endpoints rely on OS user permissions.
verify: Listener side: `(auth, peer) => principalId` validating the client credential; throw to reject.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Opens a Runtime Peer to another process. Choose one source: `spawn` starts and owns a child, `connect` dials a running service, and `listen` binds an accepting endpoint. A library-launched child may omit the source to connect back. Spawn/connect/child discovery resolves after readiness; listen resolves after binding, before any client must arrive.

sections.title: 上手

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
options: See `IRuntimeProcessPeerOptions`: source, `provide`, `report` (default `defaultRpcReporter`), `token`, `verify`, `connectTimeoutMs`, `defaultTimeoutMs` (default `30000`) and Core Peer options.
An `IRuntimeTypedPeer<TRemote>`. `close()` stops new work and drains/closes under the owning runtime budget, normally `5000` ms narrowed by remaining stop time; it does not guarantee uncooperative calls finish. Spawn ownership also stops its child.
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
Keep an existing endpoint composition for the acquired process channel; use its actual codec, framer and flow-control features.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
`defaultRpcReporter`, which reports through the default console path.
Route native process and background diagnostics to the application sink without printing credentials.
keyFactory: Application key generator for automatically keyed idempotent requests on managed spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core Peer assembly and do not consume this proxy field.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.

retryPort: Whole-invocation dispatch port for managed spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core Peer assembly and do not consume this field.

spawn: Child to start and own: `URL`, path (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (current entry), a short object `{ entry | command, args?, wrap?, wire?, ... }`, or a full `ISpawnProcessPluginDeployment`.

connect: Running service to dial: a name (`math-service`), `tcp://127.0.0.1:port`, a Unix path, or a full connect deployment.
listen: Address or name to accept sessions on; each session is its own connection.

verify: Listener side: `(auth, peer) => principalId` validating the client credential; throw to reject.

Not set: the `token` comparison is used.

symbols.purpose: Establishes a raw byte channel with its explicit handshake policy, or a message channel with matching static profiles; used in establish of full sources.
symbols.core:
channel: Raw channel from a launcher handle, `dialProcessByteChannel` or stdio.
options: `IProcessByteOptions`: `role`, `offer`, `peerId`, `auth` (responder), `scheduler`, `signal`, `ipc`, `report`.
The established channel; bad credentials throw `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`, slow handshakes `PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`.
peerId: Caller-selected remote routing identity, usually from the launched process or received bootstrap; a negotiated runtime identity may supersede it.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
signal: Caller-owned IAbortSignal cancelling this handshake attempt; later connection ownership remains with the returned channel.
Omitted: no external abort listener is attached.
handshakeTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative handshake budget in milliseconds; expiration rejects with PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT.
10000 ms for the Core byte or message handshake.
scheduler: Caller-selected IScheduler providing monotonic time and handshake timers, forwarded to the established endpoint.
Core systemScheduler.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
Send secondary failures to the application diagnostic sink while preserving the original error identity.
ipc: Caller-authored connection and session labels plus the logging port; stderr and queue limits are optional.
Correlate connection records and configure queue capacity without treating diagnostic labels as credentials.
role: Explicit local handshake role: initiator sends an offer, while responder supplies both an offer and an authentication decision.
Start the byte handshake using this side’s explicit offer.
Answer the byte handshake and enforce the declared auth policy.
Use initiator on the dialing or launching side and responder on the byte receiver; both sides supply an offer.
offer: Local `IRpcHandshakeOffer` returned by the selected offer preparation helper or authored from `@migaia/rpc-contract` policy; both roles must supply it.
auth: Responder-only authentication union: mode required invokes `verify(auth, peer)` with portable credentials and handshake peer metadata; return a principal string or void, synchronously or asynchronously. Throw/rejection refuses the handshake. Mode none explicitly skips authentication.
auth.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
Verified principal string or void, optionally promised; a failure rejects the handshake.
Require verification on externally reachable byte channels; select none only when the carrier is already private and owned.
staticAgreement: Fixed capabilities agreed by both sides (no negotiation).
ipc.connectionId: Caller-issued non-secret identifier for this physical connection, copied into diagnostic records.
ipc.sessionId: Caller-issued identifier for this logical session, allowing records from one session to be correlated.
ipc.processId: Optional process label issued by the caller for diagnostic correlation; it grants no authentication authority.
Omitted: records have no process label.
ipc.maxPendingData: Maximum queued data frames in the canonical Core send queue; separate control capacity remains available.
256 pending data frames.
ipc.maxPendingControl: Maximum queued control frames in the canonical Core send queue, independent of data-frame capacity.
8 pending control frames.
ipc.log: Callback receiving each Core IIpcLogRecord; synchronous throws and Promise rejections enter the original reporter boundary.
ipc.log.record: Structured, connection-labelled IPC record supplied by Core.
Void or Promise<void>; asynchronous completion is observed by the logging owner.
Collect structured connection records; keep secret bytes out of the sink and let report observe sink failures.
ipc.stderr: Subscription callback for child stderr bytes. The diagnostic bridge records bounded redacted summaries rather than the raw text.
ipc.stderr.listener: Bridge callback receiving each Uint8Array chunk from the child.
Unsubscribe function owned and invoked by the connection cleanup.
Omitted: no child-stderr subscription is attached.
Borrow the existing child stderr subscription for bounded redacted diagnostics and unsubscribe during channel cleanup.
auth.mode: Explicit responder authentication policy; initiator options carry no auth decision object.
Verify initiator credentials and reject throw or rejection.
Explicitly perform the handshake without credential verification.
Choose required for credential verification; none explicitly omits verification on an already private carrier.
auth.verify: Required-mode responder callback receiving remote portable auth and IRpcPeerInfo; return a principal string or void, synchronously or by Promise. Failure rejects authentication.
auth.verify.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.verify.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
staticAgreement.local: Caller-authored local static message profile, declared before any message transport activation.
staticAgreement.peer: Caller-authored expected peer profile; codec and capability order must exactly match the local profile.
staticAgreement.local.codec: This transport already delivers complete messages. Set the local codec to identity, which passes native message values through without converting them to bytes. A byte codec is rejected during configuration, before the transport is activated.
Sends each original message value unchanged. Choose identity for the local side because the underlying transport already preserves message boundaries.
Use identity on both profiles when the native carrier already preserves complete messages.
staticAgreement.local.capabilities: Lists the communication capabilities this local endpoint declares, in their fixed order. Use the same entries and order in the expected peer profile. This complete-message path does not negotiate a different list during setup.
staticAgreement.peer.codec: Set the expected peer codec to identity as well, meaning the peer sends message values without byte encoding. A different peer codec cannot match this complete-message transport and is rejected during configuration.
Requires the peer to send unchanged message values too. This matches the local format; a byte-encoded peer format would not match.
staticAgreement.peer.capabilities: Lists the capabilities expected from the peer. Every entry and its position must match the local list. If a capability is missing or differently ordered, this message-transport path cannot negotiate a correction.

256 pending data frames.
ipc.maxPendingControl: Maximum queued control frames in the canonical Core send queue, independent of data-frame capacity.
8 pending control frames.
ipc.log: Callback receiving each Core IIpcLogRecord; synchronous throws and Promise rejections enter the original reporter boundary.

Void or Promise<void>; asynchronous completion is observed by the logging owner.
Collect structured connection records; keep secret bytes out of the sink and let report observe sink failures.

ipc.stderr.listener: Bridge callback receiving each Uint8Array chunk from the child.

Omitted: no child-stderr subscription is attached.

auth.mode: Explicit responder authentication policy; initiator options carry no auth decision object.
Verify initiator credentials and reject throw or rejection.
Explicitly perform the handshake without credential verification.
Choose required for credential verification; none explicitly omits verification on an already private carrier.

auth.verify.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.verify.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
staticAgreement.local: Caller-authored local static message profile, declared before any message transport activation.
staticAgreement.peer: Caller-authored expected peer profile; codec and capability order must exactly match the local profile.

Sends each original message value unchanged. Choose identity for the local side because the underlying transport already preserves message boundaries.
Use identity on both profiles when the native carrier already preserves complete messages.
staticAgreement.local.capabilities: Lists the communication capabilities this local endpoint declares, in their fixed order. Use the same entries and order in the expected peer profile. This complete-message path does not negotiate a different list during setup.
staticAgreement.peer.codec: Set the expected peer codec to identity as well, meaning the peer sends message values without byte encoding. A different peer codec cannot match this complete-message transport and is rejected during configuration.
Requires the peer to send unchanged message values too. This matches the local format; a byte-encoded peer format would not match.
staticAgreement.peer.capabilities: Lists the capabilities expected from the peer. Every entry and its position must match the local list. If a capability is missing or differently ordered, this message-transport path cannot negotiate a correction.

signal: Caller-owned IAbortSignal cancelling this handshake attempt; later connection ownership remains with the returned channel.
Omitted: no external abort listener is attached.
handshakeTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative millisecond budget for the initial JSON-RPC bridge handshake; it does not bound later method calls.
10000 ms from JsonRpcLimit.handshakeMs.
scheduler: Required caller-selected IScheduler for handshake deadline and established connection tasks; no clock is inferred by this bridge.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
Send secondary failures to the application diagnostic sink while preserving the original error identity.
ipc: Caller-authored connection and session labels plus the logging port; stderr and queue limits are optional.

byte: Caller-owned ordered IProcessByteChannel returned by a launcher, socket adapter or stdio wrapper, with kind byte.
target: Explicit plugin contract or host catalog target: plugin requires contract only, while host requires catalog only. Stream declarations are rejected.
offer: Caller-authored native offer without auth or codecs. The bridge inserts the token, JSON codec and required JSON-RPC capabilities.
token: Nonempty credential issued by the deployment owner and expected by the JSON-RPC peer; copied into the bridge handshake, never diagnostic output.
wallClock: Required caller-selected IWallClock supplying timestamp() for outgoing JSON-RPC message sentAt metadata, distinct from monotonic scheduling.

symbols.name: IProcessPlugin
symbols.purpose: Plugin returned by `createProcessPlugin()` with a full deployment.
symbols.core:
replace: Replaces the child process while the Host keeps running. Choose stop-then-start to stop the old child before starting its replacement, or start-then-switch to start the replacement before switching over. The complete deployment example above demonstrates replacement; inspect the returned strategy and outcome.
replace.options: `{ spec?, strategy? }`, default {}. strategy defaults to stop-then-start; start-then-switch requires the real Host replace port and capacity for overlapping processes. Omitted spec reuses the deployment spec. Explicit spec includes command, args, env.inherit/set, stdio.stdin/stdout/stderr and the same token bootstrap; optional cwd/limits/permissions remain under supervision. Only the installed current definition may replace.
stop-then-start returns { strategy, outcome }, with outcome.kind replaced, rejected or failed; start-then-switch returns { strategy, plugin } after Host replacement. This complete Node file prints 42, stop-then-start and replaced: it proves native replacement readiness, not automatic proxy rebinding. The advanced facade takes an argument array [21], unlike typed Peer.request with a scalar payload.

symbols.core:
name: Plugin name in the host.
Configure this part of the advanced pricing deployment.
contract: Declared remote methods.

resilience: Caller-owned governance from createProcessResilience, borrowed by this plugin rather than closed with it.

host: Host port used to install and replace the plugin.
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.

endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Required in the full deployment overload; no endpoint factory is inferred.
Build the explicit full-deployment endpoint from this acquired channel; retain its pipeline and flow-control features.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
Send secondary failures to the application diagnostic sink while preserving the original error identity.
keyFactory: Synchronous callback returning an idempotency key when the full deployment remote proxy automatically keys an idempotent call.
Application-issued string key for that call.
Omitted: the proxy uses defaultRpcId.
Issue an application key for a declared idempotent proxy call when the caller supplies no explicit key.
retryPort: Caller-provided IRemoteRetryPort dispatching full-deployment proxy retries through the original binding.
Omitted: createRemoteRetryPort uses the binding events, scheduler and reporter.
deployment: Spawn or connect deployment.

The [terminal-child case](/en/docs/rpc-process/api/createProcessResilience#rpc-process-index--createProcessResilience--case-2) shows how to attach the original supervisor and release its resources separately; the factory example introduces the required dependencies and policies.
symbols.core:
sessionOptions: Builds result-deduplication settings and call limits for one accepted session. Result deduplication lets retries of an identified operation reuse its stored outcome. Pass the session identity received by listenRegistrations; its listener example below shows how to obtain that identity.
sessionOptions.identity: `{ connectionId, sessionId, principalId, processId? }`: accepted connection labels; principalId must be a nonempty verified principal. processId defaults to undefined. This method derives options and does not authenticate. The returned scope accepts { token, senderId }, but partitions by principalId under this governor.
`{ idempotency, limits }`.
listenRegistrations: Accepts registrations of remote processes on an address.
listenRegistrations.options: `IProcessRegistrationListenOptions`.
A listener with `address` and `close()`.
attachRegistration: Registers a supervised process with this failure-management object. The supervisor starts and restarts the process; this registration adds reporting and eventual removal if recovery fails. Supply the binding and cleanup owner shown in the complete usage example above.
attachRegistration.name: Registration name, the plugin `name`.
attachRegistration.binding: `ownership` is spawn-owned or connection-borrowed; `health` is ping, custom or none; both are required. supervisor supplies restart(), inspect(), dispose() and onTerminal(listener). The example forwards methods to the original process supervisor.
attachRegistration.liquidation: Required owner union: standalone-host supplies release(): Promise<void>; proxy-plugin supplies the same registration name and actual Host with unUse. It runs on liquidation, not ordinary registration.close().
An `IProcessRegistration`.
callGuard: Returns a stable check for this registration: terminal state refuses new calls, and liquidation keeps refusing them through the retained diagnostic record. Run guard.beforeDispatch() before each dispatch; bypassing it skips this check. Terminal is not permanent disposal and can still admit an explicit restart.
callGuard.name: Registration name. Invoke `beforeDispatch({ method, mode, generation })` before work: method is the remote path, generation is the actual supervisor generation, and mode is request, one-way, generator, async-generator or host-control; the example uses request.

inspect: Reads the current state of one registration by id. Use it when an application needs a point-in-time view without retaining the registration object. It returns undefined for an unknown id. The example above compares this view with registration.inspect().
inspect.id: Registration id.

onTerminal: Subscribes to terminal entries reported by the actual supervisor and receives the registration snapshot. This observes the current terminal state rather than declaring the process permanently unrecoverable. The returned function removes this observer; call it during cleanup.
onTerminal.listener: Receives a registration snapshot and returns void or Promise<void>; one fulfilled handler marks this report handled and stops subsequent ticks. Rejection is reported. The returned unsubscribe is separate from closing governance.
An unsubscribe function.
close: Stops this failure-management object, closes listeners it owns and detaches its registrations. symbols.name: IRuntimeDetail
symbols.purpose: Result of `peer.describe()`: this side identity, its methods and its connections.
symbols.core:
methods: Method paths provided by this local Peer; each connection detail separately lists its accepted remote methods.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` of this Peer.
self: Same identity, as given by the `self` option or generated.
provide: Method paths this side provides.
connections: Details of every connection (`IRuntimeConnectionDetail`).
unit: Unavailable for a local Peer; see `connections`.
health: A local Peer may have several connections, so this field does not combine them into one health result. It returns an unavailable value. Inspect each connection to see whether that connection is healthy.
restartCount: Restart counts describe individual connections, not the local Peer as a whole. This field returns an unavailable value. Inspect the relevant connection when you need its restart count.
resources: Resource measurements belong to the execution unit behind each connection. The local Peer returns an unavailable value here rather than a combined measurement. Inspect a connection for the resource information its runtime supports.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

blocks.text: 本包 source 为 RPC_PROCESS_ERROR_SOURCE（@migaia/rpc/process）。同步 spawn、Unix listener 准备/bind 在原错误上附语义码，保留原生类型、stack 和其它 OS 字段，原 errno code 归入语义 code；包装失败仍经 cause 可达。不要按错误 message 做控制。

rows: 握手未完成 / 凭据拒绝，修正来源和认证
已关闭或资源/close 观察者清理失败，查 cause/errors
拨号/启动或监听准备/bind失败
来源、插件或 Host 配置不合法
facade 已开始释放，需新 owner
治理配置非法 / 接入、速率、payload 提供前拒绝
共享实例显式健康隔离 / native ping 失败
终态拒新调用 / 已清算不能重启

symbols.purpose: Table of the stable error codes of this package; values are the strings on `error.code`.
symbols.core:
usageSampleFailed: `PROCESS_USAGE_SAMPLE_FAILED`: CPU or memory sampling failed; show unavailable.
hostInvalidOption: `PROCESS_HOST_INVALID_OPTION`: a host option is invalid; fix the named field.
hostClosed: `PROCESS_HOST_CLOSED`: the outlet is releasing; use a new host or Peer.
handshakeTimeout: `PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`: the handshake did not finish in time; open a new channel.
authRejected: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`: the credential was refused; do not retry with it.
channelClosed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED`: work on a closed channel; reconnect and reconcile.
connectFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`: connecting to the other process, starting it, or setting up part of the channel failed. If the system call that starts the process or opens its streams throws, you get that same error object with its type, stack and fields intact. Its `source` becomes this package and its system `code` (such as `ENOENT`) becomes `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`, one stable value to check. An already wrapped failure keeps the original on `cause`.
listenFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED`: preparing to listen, or binding the listening address, failed. You receive the same system error object, with its type, stack and other fields unchanged; it only gains this package as `source` and `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED` as `code`. Both the reported error and the rejected promise keep the original `cause` chain.
pluginInvalidOption: `PROCESS_PLUGIN_INVALID_OPTION`: a plugin or source option is invalid.
resilienceInvalidOption: `PROCESS_RESILIENCE_INVALID_OPTION`: a governance limit is invalid.
connectionLimit: `PROCESS_CONNECTION_LIMIT`: connection, rate or payload limit; the call did not run.
instanceUnhealthy: `PROCESS_INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY`: the target is suspended until a healthy replacement is ready.
healthPingFailed: `PROCESS_HEALTH_PING_FAILED`: a health ping failed; supervision restarts it.
terminalCall: `PROCESS_TERMINAL_CALL`: the registration is terminal and refuses calls.
liquidated: `PROCESS_LIQUIDATED`: the registration was liquidated; create a new one.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this const.

members.description: An enabled native health ping returned false before its supervision deadline; the owner must * restart the unit.

members.name: terminalCall
members.description: A terminal registration rejects new remote calls before they reach its inactive generation.

members.name: liquidated
members.description: A liquidated registration cannot restart; the caller must create a new registration.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
port: One end of a `MessageChannel`; it stays owned by the caller.
peerId: Instance id of the other side, taken from the `self.instanceId` that side configured.
options: `{ scheduler, capabilities? }`; pass `context.capabilities` received in `connect(context)` to negotiate extensions.
The channel (sync for the fixed profile, a Promise when extensions are negotiated).
scheduler: Clock and timers, shared with the source.
capabilities: Local capability proposal; extensions wait for the other side acknowledgement.
Not set: fixed basic profile, synchronous.

declaredConfiguration.name: capabilities
declaredConfiguration.description: Omission selects the synchronous fixed profile. Explicit fixed-profile subsets remain synchronous; runtime extensions await Core's actual bilateral ACK and cannot assert trust.

declaredConfiguration.name: scheduler
declaredConfiguration.description: Required borrowed scheduler; use the same instance as the owning supervisor and budget.

symbols.name: createThreadPeer
symbols.purpose: Opens a Runtime Peer to a Worker. In the parent, `spawn` starts the Worker (URL, path, `true` for the current entry, or a full source). Inside a library-launched Worker, calling it without a source connects back to the parent. Resolves after handshake.
symbols.core:
options: See `IRuntimeThreadPeerOptions`: `spawn` or `connect`, `provide`, `report` (default `defaultRpcReporter`), `defaultTimeoutMs` (default `30000`), `authentication`, `providerLimits`, `self` and `probe`.
runtime: Advanced: custom Node `worker_threads` resource; default the real module.
An `IRuntimeTypedPeer<TRemote>`; `close()` drains under its owner budget and requests termination of an owned Worker. Bad configuration rejects with `INVALID_CONFIG`. Explicitly unsupported exit observation, including Deno and browser Web Workers, immediately reports supervision `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` and retains an abandoned lease without waiting for the reap window. Bun and Node keep their observable exit paths.
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
Use it only when the application already owns advanced endpoint assembly for the acquired channel. The callback receives the construction signal and must return a real IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure rolls back construction; omission uses canonical assembly.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
Use the report session’s signing and verification policy when both channel ends require authenticated traffic. openSignedReportChannel supplies the matching remote configuration. Omission adds no authentication middleware.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
`defaultRpcReporter`.
Set a sink when the application needs to collect background or contained failures separately from request rejections. Omitting it uses defaultRpcReporter and console.error; it does not make a failed request successful.
keyFactory: Advanced remote-proxy key callback returning an application string for automatically keyed retry paths. The direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read this inherited field itself.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
Use it on managed proxy paths that generate keys for retryable calls. A borrowed direct connect/listen peer does not read it. Omission uses defaultRpcId in proxy paths and leaves direct call-option keys unchanged.
retryPort: Advanced application-supplied retry dispatch port for remote-proxy paths; it receives the original retry input and returns the selected dispatch result. Direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read it itself.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
connect: Application-supplied Core source callback that opens a borrowed channel; select exactly one source.
Omitted: no custom connection source.
listen: Application-supplied Core source callback accepting channel sessions; cannot be combined with another source.
Omitted: no custom listening source.
spawn: Worker to start: `URL`, path string (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (the current entry), `{ entry, base?, name?, data?, limits? }`, or a full source.
Not set: inside a library Worker connects to the parent; otherwise `connect` is needed.

Move CPU-heavy parsing, compression or image work off the main thread.
Call Worker functions with types instead of hand-written `postMessage` dispatch.
Process isolation (crash containment, separate permissions): use `@migaia/rpc-process`.
`SharedArrayBuffer` / `Atomics` shared memory: rejected.

runtime: IThreadRuntimeResource (optional)

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Opens a Runtime Peer to a Worker. In the parent, `spawn` starts the Worker (URL, path, `true` for the current entry, or a full source). Inside a library-launched Worker, calling it without a source connects back to the parent. Resolves after handshake.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import createThreadPeer from @migaia/rpc-threads, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use createThreadPeer when its function contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when createThreadPeer does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content:
Move CPU-heavy parsing, compression or image work off the main thread.
Call Worker functions with types instead of hand-written `postMessage` dispatch.
Process isolation (crash containment, separate permissions): use `@migaia/rpc-process`.
`SharedArrayBuffer` / `Atomics` shared memory: rejected.

declaredConfiguration.name: report
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional diagnostics sink; ordinary root construction defaults to Core's defaultRpcReporter.

declaredConfiguration.name: spawn
declaredConfiguration.description: Owned Worker source: callback, full deployment, short object, true, or an entry URL/path.

declaredConfiguration.name: endpointFactory
declaredConfiguration.description: A custom runtime assembly receives only the operations held by this channel view.

declaredConfiguration.name: self
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional local identity; omission generates an instance id with the display name peer.

declaredConfiguration.name: provide
declaredConfiguration.description: Explicit nested own-data method groups; defaults to no application methods and rejects * accessors during compilation.

declaredConfiguration.name: connect
declaredConfiguration.description: Connected source opener; exactly one source is required.

declaredConfiguration.name: listen
declaredConfiguration.description: Listener source opener; exactly one source is required.

declaredConfiguration.name: providerLimits
declaredConfiguration.description: Provider quotas, defaulting to 256 global and 64 per verified peer.

declaredConfiguration.name: authentication
declaredConfiguration.description: Existing per-frame credentials enable signed native transfer without a custom endpoint.

declaredConfiguration.name: probe
declaredConfiguration.description: Installs an endpoint-local synchronous observer without changing pipeline selection.

declaredConfiguration.name: defaultTimeoutMs
declaredConfiguration.description: Only request/stream inherit this positive default in their original timeout scope.

declaredConfiguration.name: contract
declaredConfiguration.description: Explicit advanced schema, modes and idempotency retain their original contract owner.

declaredConfiguration.name: keyFactory
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional idempotency key generator; omission uses the canonical identity generator.

declaredConfiguration.name: retryPort
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional whole-invocation retry policy; omission sends once.

symbols.purpose: Creates a plugin that installs one Worker connection into a PluginHost; the host owns and releases it and gains the `host.thread` outlet.
symbols.core:
options: Same `spawn` / `provide` as `createThreadPeer`, plus `name` (connection name in the host) and optional `expose` (host method paths the Worker may call).
runtime: Advanced: custom Node `worker_threads` resource.
A plugin for `host.use()`.
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
Use it only when the application already owns advanced endpoint assembly for the acquired channel. The callback receives the construction signal and must return a real IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure rolls back construction; omission uses canonical assembly.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
Use the report session’s signing and verification policy when both channel ends require authenticated traffic. openSignedReportChannel supplies the matching remote configuration. Omission adds no authentication middleware.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
Connect the export monitor when a report plugin needs message activity observations. The callback forwards events to the application sink; omission installs no observer.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
`defaultRpcReporter`.
Set a sink when the application needs to collect background or contained failures separately from request rejections. Omitting it uses defaultRpcReporter and console.error; it does not make a failed request successful.
keyFactory: Advanced remote-proxy key callback returning an application string for automatically keyed retry paths. The direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read this inherited field itself.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
Use it on managed proxy paths that generate keys for retryable calls. A borrowed direct connect/listen peer does not read it. Omission uses defaultRpcId in proxy paths and leaves direct call-option keys unchanged.
retryPort: Advanced application-supplied retry dispatch port for remote-proxy paths; it receives the original retry input and returns the selected dispatch result. Direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read it itself.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
connect: Application-supplied Core source callback that opens a borrowed channel; select exactly one source.
Omitted: no custom connection source.
listen: Application-supplied Core source callback accepting channel sessions; cannot be combined with another source.
Omitted: no custom listening source.
spawn: Worker to start: `URL`, path string (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (the current entry), `{ entry, base?, name?, data?, limits? }`, or a full source.
Not set: inside a library Worker connects to the parent; otherwise `connect` is needed.
name: Caller-selected nonempty registration name copied when constructing the cold plugin; use the same name when addressing the installed runtime outlet.
expose: Distinct nonempty paths explicitly exposing current Host feature methods, runtime connection routes or the reserved host control entry. Only this snapshotted whitelist becomes remotely callable.
Omitted: an empty whitelist; only provide methods are published.
host: The same actual PluginHost handle into which this plugin is installed, supplying use, unUse, plugin and revision for explicit host exposure.
Omitted: allowed unless expose contains host; explicit host exposure requires host, catalog and resolvePlugin together.
catalog: Application-authored IRemoteHostCatalog declaring the only plugin contracts available through explicitly exposed host control.
Omitted: no host-control catalog; required when expose contains host.
resolvePlugin: Synchronous local resolver invoked by the canonical host-control owner after catalog admission; definitions remain local and are installed through the original Host.
resolvePlugin.name: Plugin name admitted by the declared catalog.
resolvePlugin.config: Optional portable configuration from the remote host-use request.
Local plugin definition accepted by the Host; a thrown error rejects the host-use request.
Omitted: no local resolver; required when expose contains host.
After installation the host has `host.thread`: calls to the Worker by connection name, queries (`list`, `get`), `broadcast`, lifecycle control (`stop`, `kill`, `restart`, `replace`) and events (`on`, `watch`). The host disposes the Worker with itself.

Manage several Workers in one host and restart them from an admin panel.

symbols.name: IRuntimeDetail
symbols.purpose: Result of `peer.describe()`: this side identity, its methods and its connections.
symbols.core:
methods: Method paths provided by this local Peer; each connection detail separately lists its accepted remote methods.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` of this Peer.
self: Same identity, as given by the `self` option or generated.
provide: Method paths this side provides.
connections: Details of every connection (`IRuntimeConnectionDetail`).
unit: Unavailable for a local Peer; see `connections`.
health: A local Peer may have several connections, so this field does not combine them into one health result. It returns an unavailable value. Inspect each connection to see whether that connection is healthy.
restartCount: Restart counts describe individual connections, not the local Peer as a whole. This field returns an unavailable value. Inspect the relevant connection when you need its restart count.
resources: Resource measurements belong to the execution unit behind each connection. The local Peer returns an unavailable value here rather than a combined measurement. Inspect a connection for the resource information its runtime supports.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

symbols.name: IRuntimeThreadPeerOptions
symbols.purpose: Options of `createThreadPeer()`: the Worker source plus the Core Peer options.
symbols.core:
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
Use it only when the application already owns advanced endpoint assembly for the acquired channel. The callback receives the construction signal and must return a real IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure rolls back construction; omission uses canonical assembly.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
Use the report session’s signing and verification policy when both channel ends require authenticated traffic. openSignedReportChannel supplies the matching remote configuration. Omission adds no authentication middleware.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
`defaultRpcReporter`.
Set a sink when the application needs to collect background or contained failures separately from request rejections. Omitting it uses defaultRpcReporter and console.error; it does not make a failed request successful.
keyFactory: Advanced remote-proxy key callback returning an application string for automatically keyed retry paths. The direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read this inherited field itself.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
Use it on managed proxy paths that generate keys for retryable calls. A borrowed direct connect/listen peer does not read it. Omission uses defaultRpcId in proxy paths and leaves direct call-option keys unchanged.
retryPort: Advanced application-supplied retry dispatch port for remote-proxy paths; it receives the original retry input and returns the selected dispatch result. Direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read it itself.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
connect: Application-supplied Core source callback that opens a borrowed channel; select exactly one source.
Omitted: no custom connection source.
listen: Application-supplied Core source callback accepting channel sessions; cannot be combined with another source.
Omitted: no custom listening source.
spawn: Worker to start: `URL`, path string (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (the current entry), `{ entry, base?, name?, data?, limits? }`, or a full source.
Not set: inside a library Worker connects to the parent; otherwise `connect` is needed.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.

symbols.name: IRuntimeTypedPeer
symbols.purpose: A Runtime Peer typed by `TRemote`: method names, payloads and results are checked against the other side API. Also has `self`, `describe()`, `outcome()`, `on()` and `close()`.
symbols.core:
self: Frozen local peer name and instanceId minted or supplied during this connection construction; it is not a remote authentication principal.
outcome: Queries the original remote operation ledger for a prior idempotency key, without dispatching that operation again.
outcome.idempotencyKey: The caller-issued key supplied as options.idempotencyKey on an earlier request to this connection.
Promise of IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult; support and availability come from the accepted remote runtime contract.
describe: Queries the local accepted peer detail asynchronously. Without format returns IRuntimeDetail; json, yaml or toml returns the admitted text projection. It does not claim unavailable physical metrics.
describe.options: Optional query format from IRuntimeQueryOptions; omitted returns the object snapshot.
Promise of local detail or formatted text, following the selected query format.
on: Registers a future RuntimeEventName listener after construction; factory resolution already represents initial readiness. Listener return is ignored and failures are contained by the runtime reporter.
on.event: A RuntimeEventName value such as ready or exit; it selects future connection lifecycle notifications.
on.listener: Callback receives IRuntimeEvent from this connection; return is ignored and throws or rejected thenables are reported.
Idempotent removal function for this registration; closing the peer clears its publisher.
close: Ends this logical connection and releases its owned channel resources; platform factories also terminate a worker or child they spawned.
Shared completion Promise retaining the original close operation identity; no new calls are admitted once closing begins.
[Symbol.asyncDispose]: Scoped asynchronous cleanup is the exact original close operation, including its Promise identity.
The same completion Promise as close(), including platform-owned resource cleanup.
request: Calls a method the other side provides and waits for its result. Default deadline 30000 ms (`defaultTimeoutMs`); errors keep their native type and `(source, code)`.
request.method: Dotted path of a method in the other side `provide`, e.g. `math.double`.
request.args: `(payload?, options?)`: one payload and call options (`timeoutMs`, `signal`, `transfer`, `idempotencyKey`).
The method result, typed from `TRemote`.
notify: Sends a one-way call; no result comes back.
notify.method: Dotted method path provided by the other side.
notify.args: `(payload?, options?)` as for `request`.
Resolves once the call was sent.
stream: Calls a method that returns an iterable and yields its items as they arrive.
stream.method: Dotted path of an iterator method provided by the other side.
stream.args: `(payload?, options?)` as for `request`.
An async iterator of the yielded items.
group: Sends several calls as one batch and returns the outcome of each step in order.
group.steps: Steps `{ method, payload? }` in order.
group.options: Batch options such as `timeoutMs` and `signal`.
One outcome per step (success value or error).

blocks.text: Node launcher 的原生 Worker 构造参数被拒绝时，使用 Core INVALID_CONFIG 标识；若已有原生 code，则以包装错误保留原 Error、name、message、stack 和原生 code 于 cause，不覆盖它们。此分类只描述 Node 构造边界，不泛化为所有 Web 构造器异常。

本包本地错误码对象 RpcThreadErrorCode 只有 usageSampleFailed，值为 THREAD_USAGE_SAMPLE_FAILED，RPC_THREAD_ERROR_SOURCE 为 @migaia/rpc/threads。调用、监督和 Host 边界各使用自己的 source，不把所有失败改成本包采样码。按 source / code 分支，不匹配 message 文本；业务异常跨 Worker 后保留原生类型、message、stack、source/code 与 cause / errors 链，不能承诺接收端对象与发送端同一 identity。
Worker 单独运行配置失败通常是没有库 launcher bootstrap；默认 buffer 未失效是复制语义；Worker 是否重启取决于 restart 策略。需人工恢复时用 Host 的 restart / replace，并查看 list / get 的当前代次与退出信息。
下表区分线程采样、监督、Core 与 Remote 的错误来源。线程 API 从 `@migaia/rpc-threads` 导入；Core 与 Remote API 分别从 `@migaia/rpc-core` 和 `@migaia/rpc-core/remote` 导入，`source` 值保留各自的错误身份。

runtimeApi: Advanced `IRuntimePeerSourceContext` supplied by the Core source owner; per-launch held metadata takes precedence over this configured context.
Omitted: only private per-launch metadata can supply runtime API bootstrap.
execArgv: Caller-selected runtime argument list copied for each native Worker. If new Worker throws synchronously, launch rejects with Core INVALID_CONFIG. An existing native code such as ERR_WORKER_INVALID_EXEC_ARGV is not overwritten: the original Error, code, name, message and stack remain on cause under the established conflict policy. This classification does not cover later asynchronous Worker business failures.
Omitted: preserve Node’s native execution-argument inheritance.

symbols.name: emitOutput
symbols.purpose: Synchronously emits a complete management projection as JSON, YAML or TOML. Copies own enumerable data without invoking getters or serialization hooks; rejects cycles, nonfinite numbers and unsupported values before producing output.
symbols.core:
value: Required caller-owned data: `null`, booleans, finite numbers, strings, dense arrays or plain/null-prototype records recursively containing these values. Own enumerable fields must be data properties; accessors, symbol keys, undefined, bigint, functions, cycles and class instances are rejected. TOML further requires a record root, no nested `null`, and Unicode scalar strings. The caller chooses field names such as `theme` and `retries`; they are not emitter options.
format: Optional `SerializeTextFormat`: `json` (the default) emits one JSON value, `yaml` emits valid flow-style YAML, and `toml` emits record assignments. These are the only three values. This selects a text emitter, not an input parser or registry plugin.
One complete string. Rejected format or graph throws native TypeError with INVALID_OPTION and no partial output.
parameters: value: unknown
format: ISerializeTextFormat (optional)
symbols.returns: string
examples:
import { emitOutput, SerializeTextFormat } from '@migaia/serialize'

const settings = { theme: 'dark', retries: 2 }
console.log('JSON:', emitOutput(settings))
console.log('YAML:', emitOutput(settings, SerializeTextFormat.yaml))
console.log('TOML:\n' + emitOutput(settings, SerializeTextFormat.toml))

guidance.id: 把同一份配置导出为三种文本格式
guidance.heading: 把同一份配置导出为三种文本格式

blocks.text: 配置下载需要 JSON、YAML 和 TOML，分别拼接文本时，对输入值的接受规则不同，同一份设置可能得到不一致的内容。
手写格式化会把值校验、引号转义和嵌套集合语法混在一起，增加格式时容易顺带改变保留哪些字段或怎样转义字符串。
把配置交给 `emitOutput()`，用 `SerializeTextFormat` 选择格式。三种格式共用普通数据接纳规则，每次调用都会先对输入校验并投影，再输出所选格式；省略格式时使用 JSON。
emitOutput 的第一个参数是普通自有数据，第二个 format 可省略，默认 json；SerializeTextFormat.yaml/toml 分别选择另外两种输出。theme 和 retries 是业务字段。格式全集为 json/yaml/toml，YAML/TOML 只生成文本，不提供反向 parser。

blocks.code:
import { emitOutput, SerializeTextFormat } from '@migaia/serialize'

const settings = { theme: 'dark', retries: 2 }
console.log('JSON:', emitOutput(settings))
console.log('YAML:', emitOutput(settings, SerializeTextFormat.yaml))
console.log('TOML:\n' + emitOutput(settings, SerializeTextFormat.toml))

blocks.text: 输出：
依次输出 `JSON: {"theme":"dark","retries":2}`、`YAML: {"theme": "dark", "retries": 2}`，然后三行 `TOML:`、`"theme" = "dark"`、`"retries" = 2`。
三种输出保留了传入字段，YAML 使用合法的流式集合语法。这是文本生成工具，不是 YAML 或 TOML 解析器。TOML 要求根值为记录并拒绝 null，其余格式也会拒绝不支持的值，不会悄悄省略。

guidance.id: 把同一份配置导出为三种文本格式
guidance.heading: 把同一份配置导出为三种文本格式

blocks.text: 配置下载需要 JSON、YAML 和 TOML，分别拼接文本时，对输入值的接受规则不同，同一份设置可能得到不一致的内容。
手写格式化会把值校验、引号转义和嵌套集合语法混在一起，增加格式时容易顺带改变保留哪些字段或怎样转义字符串。
把配置交给 `emitOutput()`，用 `SerializeTextFormat` 选择格式。三种格式共用普通数据接纳规则，每次调用都会先对输入校验并投影，再输出所选格式；省略格式时使用 JSON。
emitOutput 的第一个参数是普通自有数据，第二个 format 可省略，默认 json；SerializeTextFormat.yaml/toml 分别选择另外两种输出。theme 和 retries 是业务字段。格式全集为 json/yaml/toml，YAML/TOML 只生成文本，不提供反向 parser。

blocks.code:
import { emitOutput, SerializeTextFormat } from '@migaia/serialize'

const settings = { theme: 'dark', retries: 2 }
console.log('JSON:', emitOutput(settings))
console.log('YAML:', emitOutput(settings, SerializeTextFormat.yaml))
console.log('TOML:\n' + emitOutput(settings, SerializeTextFormat.toml))

blocks.text: 输出：
依次输出 `JSON: {"theme":"dark","retries":2}`、`YAML: {"theme": "dark", "retries": 2}`，然后三行 `TOML:`、`"theme" = "dark"`、`"retries" = 2`。
三种输出保留了传入字段，YAML 使用合法的流式集合语法。这是文本生成工具，不是 YAML 或 TOML 解析器。TOML 要求根值为记录并拒绝 null，其余格式也会拒绝不支持的值，不会悄悄省略。

symbols.name: createPortableWalker
symbols.purpose: Creates a synchronous specialized walker with policy callbacks captured once. The returned callable projects a value and byte metadata; its value method avoids metadata collection. Policy callbacks own validation and coded errors, and traversal owns cycle tracking.
symbols.core:
strategy: Caller-owned IPortableWalkerStrategy with scalar, binary, record and violation hooks. Optional array, field-write and finish hooks specialize projection; callbacks are synchronous and throwing stops traversal.
A callable walker(value, active?, initialDepth?, beforeNativeBinary?) returning { value, byteUpperBound, hasBinary }, plus walker.value with the same arguments returning only the projection. Input is caller-owned, active is an optional enclosing ancestor Set, initialDepth defaults to zero, and beforeNativeBinary is an optional no-argument throwing guard exposed to policy context rather than automatically called. byteUpperBound is conservative JSON/native-byte accounting, not an encoded measurement; hasBinary records inline or native binary presence. Failures use strategy.violation.
parameters: strategy: IPortableWalkerStrategy
symbols.returns: IPortableWalker

symbols.name: ICodec
symbols.purpose: Generic synchronous codec object containing format identity, explicit version, encoded representation and two callbacks. Format factories freeze the codec object; they do not freeze decoded application data.
symbols.core:
id: Codec format identifier fixed by its factory, such as `json`, `cbor`, `message-pack`, `protobuf` or `identity`.
version: The version number supplied when creating this codec, which converts values to a data format and back. It identifies the format version that producers and consumers agree to use. The codec retains the number; changing the original construction options later does not change this property.
encodedType: Declares the runtime representation produced by encoding so a transport can admit the correct payload shape.
Identity representation preserves any input without changing object identity.
Text representation emitted by the JSON format codec.
Byte representation emitted by CBOR, MessagePack and Protobuf codecs.
encode: Synchronously converts the supplied application value to the codec representation; built-in format failures carry package codes and original causes.
encode.value: Application value admitted by this codec; portable formats accept `ICodecValue`, while Protobuf accepts its generated message shape.
The encoded `TEncoded` value; identity returns the input itself, while format codecs return text or bytes.
decode: Synchronously restores the application value from this codec representation; invalid portable data or malformed format data throws.
decode.value: Encoded value returned by the matching codec encode operation, or received from a carrier using that format and version.
The decoded `TValue`; identity returns the same object, portable formats validate the result and Protobuf returns its message shape.
symbols.advanced: A transport selects admission and wire behavior from codec metadata while keeping application types generic.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

symbols.name: IPortableWalkerStrategy
symbols.purpose: Caller-owned synchronous traversal policy captured once by createPortableWalker. Hooks receive the current node and invocation context; callbacks must return synchronously, and the violation hook throws the caller-owned coded error with the original cause.
symbols.core:
maxDepth: Maximum admitted traversal depth, where root depth defaults to zero. Finite limits must be nonnegative safe integers.
Infinity, so no strategy depth ceiling is imposed.
scalar: Synchronous hook receiving primitive candidate value and walker context. Return a primitive or { value, violation? }; a deferred violation is raised after projection, while context.reject fails immediately.
scalar.value: Primitive node supplied by traversal from the caller input graph.
scalar.context: Invocation tools: reject(reason, cause?), isAncestor(object), isUint8Array, bytesToBase64url and isCanonicalBase64url; these are synchronous and reject throws.
Projected scalar or deferred scalar result; a throw aborts the traversal.
record: Synchronous hook receiving an object and context. Return undefined for array handling, or entries with optional output. A tag emits an inline bytes object instead of traversing entries; hasBinary marks an existing binary tag, and validate checks the completed record. Entry children are traversed by the walker; missing output validates without constructing a record.
record.value: Current object node supplied by traversal.
record.context: Current invocation rejection, ancestor and binary helper tools.
Record admission or undefined. Optional validate(output) synchronously returns a violation reason or undefined; any throw aborts traversal through policy handling.

context: Caller label used in collector error context and position diagnostics.

text, returning an empty text chunk.
Return [text, empty string] when no chunks are produced.
Reject with ENCODE_FAILED when no chunks are produced.
Choose text for optional exports and reject when an empty download is a failure. Omission selects text and returns an empty string chunk.

declaredConfiguration.description: Attaches read-only `source`, `code`, and optional `context` and returns the original error. Never rebuilds or replaces the error or overwrites its stack. Idempotent for matching `(source, code)`: returns the error and adds `context` only if not already defined. Conflicting identity throws a `TypeError` instead of silently rewriting immutable properties. / export function tagSerializeError<E extends Error>( error: E, code: ISerializeErrorCode, context?: string ): ISerializeTaggedError<E> { const tagged = error as ISerializeTaggedError<E> const already = (error as { readonly source?: string }).source !== undefined if (already) { if (tagged.source === SERIALIZE_SOURCE && tagged.code === code) { if (context !== undefined && tagged.context === undefined) { Object.defineProperty(error, 'context', { value: context, enumerable: true }) } return tagged } // The canonical owner supplies the coded conflict and retains the original error as cause. return attachErrorIdentity(error, { source: SERIALIZE_SOURCE, code }) as ISerializeTaggedError<E> } attachErrorIdentity(error, { source: SERIALIZE_SOURCE, code }) if (context !== undefined) { Object.defineProperty(error, 'context', { value: context, enumerable: true }) } return tagged } /** Tags a standalone parser or conversion failure without rebuilding an annotatable native error. Host codes or immutable errors need a coded TypeError wrapper; the exact original remains cause. The utils attachment hooks own conflict detection instead of duplicating it in each parser. / export function tagSerializeFailure( error: unknown, code: ISerializeErrorCode, message: string ): Error { if (!isNativeErrorValue(error)) return createSerializeError(code, message, { cause: error }) return attachErrorIdentity( error, { source: SERIALIZE_SOURCE, code }, { onConflict: () => createSerializeTypeError(code, message, { cause: error }), onFailure: () => createSerializeTypeError(code, message, { cause: error }) } ) } /** Creates a native construction or lifecycle error, such as `REGISTRY_DISPOSED`, `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`, or rollback failure. Attaches `source`, `code`, and optional `context`, `cause`, and `errors`. `errors` is a frozen snapshot copied after rollback completes. An empty list omits that property and never replaces `cause`. / export function createSerializeError( code: ISerializeErrorCode, message: string, options?: { /** Original non-undefined failure retained through Error.cause.

blocks.text: SerializeCodecError(message, details) 的 details 必含 code、type、phase、chunkIndex、bytesConsumed，可选 context、source、cause；source 默认 @migaia/serialize，TCode 默认 ISerializeErrorCode，上层可用自己的 code 联合与 source 复用它。phase 为 encode/decode，cause 保留原对象。registry 编解码失败和原生构造/生命周期失败载体不同，统一按 (source, code) 判断，不能只靠 instanceof。

rows: ENCODE_FAILED：编码、空输出或流迭代失败；cause 保留原错。
INVALID_CHUNK：tuple/标签/数据错、value 混流或转 wire。
ABORTED：协作式取消；可能为 SerializeCodecError 或 tagged 原生错误，取决于边界。
INVALID_OPTION：插件、版本、portable、scheduler、流选项、Base64 或输出准入非法。
ENV_UNSUPPORTED：Encoding 等必需宿主能力缺失。

blocks.text: tagSerializeError(error, code, context?) 返回原错误并附只读 source/code，context 未提供保持未设；同身份重复附加幂等，context 仅补一次。冲突委托 utils，抛 (@migaia/utils, ERROR_IDENTITY_CONFLICT)，原错误在 cause，不能静默改写身份。

ISerializeTaggedError 为原生错误附 source/code/context 的类型；ISerializeTypeError、ISerializeRangeError 保持各自原生类型，ISerializeLifecycleError 另允许 errors。createSerializeError、createSerializeTypeError、createSerializeRangeError 分别构造带码 Error/TypeError/RangeError；code/message 必填，options 默认未提供，均允许 cause/context，普通 Error 另允许 errors 的冻结快照。错误码是公开 API，错误 factory 不改写 stack。空输出进度为 0；decode 坏 chunk 进度为 0；decode parser 原错携带该段字节数；外层 stream 重新包装保留自己的片序，不丢掉内层原因。
value 不能转文本/字节或混用时应回到业务对象处理；CODEC_NOT_FOUND 先检查 types 与存档的 type；REGISTRY_DISPOSED 需要新 registry；collectStream 合并含 bytes 的多段须显式 encoder。大数据仍阻塞时检查初始片大小、上下限与 yieldTo，不能把切片当作抢占式终止。

完整组合顺序为：创建 registry；逐片 encode 并交实际 sink；接收端逐片 decode；旧格式用记录的 type 读取，新写默认 primaryType；需要文本边界时再显式做 UTF-8/Base64；最后 await dispose，若设 deadline，记住它只限排空。包提供 fmt、lint、typecheck、typecheck:test、test 与单独 build，不把未复核历史测量当作性能结论。

symbols.name: decodeStream
symbols.purpose: Decodes each input chunk independently through a registry without collecting the stream. Pair with encodeStream when restoring arrays encoded in slices; it yields one decoded slice per chunk and does not merge arrays.

symbols.name: encodeStream
symbols.purpose: Adaptively slices an application array, encodes each slice through a registry and yields ordered chunks with bounded in-flight encoding. Pair it with a registry created by `createSerializeRegistry` and an installed parser such as `jsonPlugin`; the example consumes each chunk directly with `chunkToText`. A receiver can instead use `decodeStream` to restore separate arrays. Concatenating JSON slice texts does not make one JSON document. The runnable case imports `@migaia/utils/scheduler` directly: install `@migaia/utils` as a direct dependency alongside this package.
symbols.core:
registry: ISerializeRegistry created by createSerializeRegistry with the desired parser plugins installed.
items: Caller-owned array to divide into slices; each slice is encoded as an independent array value.
AsyncGenerator<ISerializeChunk> in original slice order. Breaking iteration cancels owned work; parser failures retain slice position and cause, while option admission uses INVALID_OPTION.
targetMs: Positive finite consumer processing budget in milliseconds; measured elapsed time adjusts the next slice size.
`8` milliseconds per slice; this is a target rather than a hard execution deadline.
minItems: Positive safe integer lower bound on items per slice, reducing overhead from very small batches.
`64` items, including the lower clamp applied to the initial slice.
maxItems: Positive safe integer upper bound on items per slice; must be at least `minItems`.
`250000` items; adaptive growth never exceeds this upper bound.
initialItems: Positive safe integer initial size before consumer timing is available; clamped between the item bounds.
`2048` items before clamping to `minItems` and `maxItems`.
yieldTo: Optional no-argument async callback invoked between slices. Resolve after yielding execution; a throw or rejection stops iteration.
A `Promise<void>` whose fulfillment permits the next slice; rejection reaches the stream consumer.
Schedules a zero-delay task with the supplied scheduler; its wait observes cancellation.
Use a host task or frame callback when consumers must let other work run between slices. The callback returns Promise<void>; rejection stops iteration. Omission schedules a zero-delay task through scheduler and observes cancellation.
signal: Caller-owned structural `IAbortSignal`, usually from `createAbortController().signal`, requests cooperative cancellation.
`undefined`: no caller cancellation signal is installed.
scheduler: Required `IScheduler`, with no default: `now()` returns finite monotonic milliseconds; `schedule(callback, delayMs)` asynchronously schedules the no-argument callback and returns a task with idempotent `cancel()` and optional `unref()`. An optional `defer(callback)` is part of the scheduler contract but is not required for slicing. Use `systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler` for host scheduling.
type: Registered format tag selected from registry.types or a stored envelope.
The registry primaryType from its first registered plugin.
context: Caller diagnostic label identifying the logical stream in errors.
The literal `stream` label is used when omitted.
maxInFlight: Positive safe integer limit on concurrent slice encoding promises; higher values overlap work while retaining more slices.
`1`, waiting for one encoded slice before admitting the next.
parameters: registry: ISerializeRegistry
items: readonly T[]
options: IEncodeStreamOptions
