members.name: notInitialized
members.description: Rejects synchronous field creation or allocation before `ensureWasm()` finishes, or after * initialization fails. First await `ensureWasm()`, or use the `StoreProvider` `ready` barrier to * finish initialization.

members.name: fieldDisposed
members.description: Rejects scalar/record value access and array data operations after field disposal. Create a new * field instead of reusing it; metadata such as disposed and fixed array length remains * readable.

members.name: initAborted
members.description: Reports field initialization cancelled through an AbortSignal. Preserve an unclassified native * reason by identity/class/stack; complete foreign identities remain with their owner, and other * reasons stay reachable through cause. Handle it as cooperative cancellation.

members.name: reservedFieldName
members.description: Rejects a `wasm.record` field named `dispose` or `disposed`. Choose a different field name.

members.name: allocationFailed
members.description: Reports no usable allocation id/pointer, failed array alignment, or corrupt stored string * length. Check allocation availability and memory integrity. Invalid requested sizes are * INVALID_OPTION rather than this allocation/memory failure.

members.name: invalidOption
members.description: Rejects invalid field construction or write arguments, including excessive length, invalid * `granularity`, out-of-range indices or ranges, or inaccessible ArrayLike length/items. Keep the * original read failure reachable. Correct the parameter instead of retrying the same invalid * input.

members.name: cleanupFailed
members.description: Reports multiple owned-resource cleanup failures during field release or construction rollback. * Inspect `AggregateError.errors`. It preserves all original cleanup failures in execution * order.

members.name: instancePoisoned
members.description: Rejects allocation after an arena export used by this package on the shared instance raised * `WebAssembly.RuntimeError` (a trap). A trap can leave the Rust arena borrow held, so every * later export would trap again; the instance is unusable for the rest of the page or process. * `cause` is the original trap. Reload the page or restart the process; retrying cannot succeed.

symbols.purpose: Resource IResourceOptions plus Runtime selection and per-fetch transfer callback; known fields are read once before Resource ownership and auto-start.
symbols.core:
debugName: Label shown in reactive diagnostics and in request error context.
Not set: diagnostics show no label.
ttl: Success lifetime in milliseconds; positive finite lifetimes revalidate on an expired read. `0` and `Infinity` disable time expiration, but changed dependencies, including after suspension, still trigger refetching. Must be ≥ 0 or `Infinity`.
`Infinity`: fresh until a dependency changes or `refetch()` is called.
autoStart: Start the first request in the constructor.
`true`: starts immediately unless the initial snapshot is fresh.
staleWhileRevalidate: Keep showing expired success data while the refresh runs (`refreshing` is `true`) instead of switching to `pending`.
`false`: an expired value is replaced by `pending`.
retry: Resource retry policy: a non-negative integer extra-attempt count, or synchronous (failureCount,error) => boolean. failureCount starts at one and error is the original fetch failure. Return true to retry; callback throws or non-boolean/thenable results become Resource failure, without awaiting a Promise.
Zero extra attempts; no automatic retry.
retryDelay: Finite non-negative milliseconds, or synchronous (failureCount,error) => milliseconds for each accepted retry. Receives the one-based count and original failure; callback throws or invalid/non-number/thenable results become Resource failure. A delayed retry remains cancellable through Resource.
Zero milliseconds; retries without a configured delay.
Use a fixed millisecond delay for short failures, or a synchronous callback for increasing waits. failureCount starts at one. Omission retries immediately; retry must also allow another attempt.
keepAlive: Keep upstream dependencies connected while nothing reads `state`, so changes are still tracked.
`false`: unobserved resources disconnect upstream.
initialSnapshot: Success snapshot from `dehydrate()` (server rendering or persistence) used as the initial state; it is revalidated when expired.
Not set: start from `idle`.
scheduler: IScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler controls Resource TTL and retry clocks; forwarded unchanged to Resource.
systemScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler.
runtime: IRuntime returned by reactive createRuntime; selectInput reads belong to this Resource Runtime. Other-Runtime reads are governed by reactive ownership checks.
Reactive defaultRuntime; pass a request/instance Runtime for isolation.
transfer: Synchronous callback receiving the selected Input and returning readonly native transfer entries for that request; it runs in the Resource fetcher after selectInput. Throws become Resource fetch failures; no Promise result is supported. Transferring may detach caller data and does not guarantee end-to-end zero-copy.
undefined: no native transfer entries.
Set it when the caller can give up native buffer ownership after sending an input. Return a synchronous transfer list; aliases can detach even if the request later fails. Omission sends no explicit list.

disposed: True after close/dispose starts, before asynchronous endpoint cleanup completes.

symbols.name: createSerializeWorkerHandler
symbols.purpose: Installs a supplied parser on the worker and handles decode responses and bounded encode streams. Pair with workerPlugin or workerParser; attach returned handler to host messages. Parser lifetime remains caller-owned.
symbols.core:
parser: ISerializeParser from @migaia/serialize/plugins or a compatible implementation. encode(value,{signal,context}) may return chunk, iterable or async iterable; decode(chunk,context) returns a value or Promise. Worker sets context to serialize-worker; parser failures use only canonical RPC rejection, retaining name, message, stack, source, code, cause and aggregate errors. Already-delivered chunks remain available before the stream reports failure.
post: Synchronous host callback receiving raw message and optional readonly transfer list; return void, normally forward to worker-global postMessage. Native send failures follow RPC transport policy.
IManagedRpcHandler callable with raw host event.data, plus close/dispose/pendingCount/disposed. Invalid or inaccessible factory parser members are INVALID_OPTION: native failures retain identity/class/stack, complete foreign identities remain unchanged, and untaggable failures remain on cause. Encode uses two initial credits and acknowledgements. Stream failure is a canonical RPC rejection; an iterator.return failure is attached with the primary first in the reachable error chain. Handler disposal does not call parser.dispose.
parameters: parser: ISerializeParser
post: (message: unknown, transfer?: readonly unknown[]) => void
symbols.returns: IManagedRpcHandler

symbols.name: createSupervisor
symbols.signature:
export declare function createSupervisor<
  TSpec,
  THandle extends IUnitHandle<TExit>,
  TExit,
  TContext extends ILaunchContext = ILaunchContext,
>(
  options: ISupervisorOptions<TSpec, THandle, TExit, TContext>,
): ISupervisor<THandle, TSpec>;
symbols.purpose: Creates a command controller around an application profile, runtime launcher and shared budget. Construction validates policy but does not start execution.
symbols.core:
An `ISupervisor`; invalid configuration throws `INVALID_OPTION`, insufficient required capabilities throw `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
Set ready when creating a handle does not yet make its service usable. Resolve after the handshake; rejection fails startup and follows restart policy. Omit it to accept launch completion as readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
Use on-failure to retry crashes but stop after normal completion. never disables automatic retries; always also restarts normal exits. Omission selects on-failure. The task follows the configured backoff when a startup attempt fails.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
Choose stay when an operator must intervene after restart exhaustion. cooldown reopens admission after afterMs. Omitting terminalPolicy keeps the stay behavior. Disposal permanently closes either policy.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
Set beforeTerminate to drain pending application work before termination. Resolve after flushing; rejection is reported and retirement continues. drainTimeoutMs, exitTimeoutMs and reapTimeoutMs bound separate phases. Omit the callback to skip draining; omitted phase limits are 5000 ms.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force. Explicitly unsupported exit observation reports EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE immediately; abandoned leases remain held until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
Set health for a service that can become unresponsive without exiting. check resolves on success; rejection or timeout counts toward failureThreshold. Reaching that threshold invalidates readiness. Omit health for no periodic checks; coroutine heartbeat cannot coexist with it.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
Keep required, the default, when requested capabilities must be enforced or monitored; weaker declarations fail construction. Choose best-effort only when weaker guarantees are acceptable. This coroutine cannot isolate faults, so its additional fault-isolation requirement appears in degraded diagnostics.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
profile: Application-supplied `IUnitProfile` owns validation, required capabilities, termination and exit classification.
hooks: Optional `ISupervisionHooks` supplied by the outer adapter for adoption, attachment and diagnostics.
Absent: no adapter extension hooks run.
parameters: options: ISupervisorOptions<TSpec, THandle, TExit, TContext>
symbols.returns: ISupervisor<THandle, TSpec>

configuration.descriptionZh: 持久回收：注入 registry，并在创建监督器或预热池之前调用 `reclaimOrphanProcesses`。回收只结束指纹仍然匹配的记录；pid 已被复用的记录只删除、不结束。失败的记录会保留，供下次再试。预热池使用和监督器相同的预算、启动器和规格对象；它启动空闲进程，但监督器取用后仍会执行就绪检查。`restart()` 和 `replace()` 会绕过过时的空闲进程。预热池和监督器使用相同的 id、registry 和 namespace 时，取用会沿用预热进程已有的持久记录及其退出清理；不同的拥有者各自登记记录。在补发缓冲输出或实时转发时，输出回调抛出的异常会被报告，但不会中断输出。registry 的 `list` 失败会以 `ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED` 收集并报告，`detail.step` 为 `list`，此时不会动任何记录。

configuration.name: restart
configuration.type: { /** Selects never, on-failure or always restart after exit; defaults to on-failure. */ readonly mode?: RestartMode; /** First automatic restart delay in scheduler milliseconds; defaults to 250. */ readonly initialDelayMs?: number; /** Multiplier for successive restart delays; defaults to 2 and remains bounded by maxDelayMs. */ readonly factor?: number; /** Upper bound on exponential restart delay in milliseconds; defaults to 30000. */ readonly maxDelayMs?: number; /** Maximum restart attempts in the sliding window before the supervisor enters terminal state. */ readonly maxRestarts?: number; /** Sliding scheduler-time window used to count restart attempts; defaults to 60000 milliseconds. */ readonly windowMs?: number; }
configuration.description: 默认值：启动时限 10 秒；启动超时与其他启动失败使用同一套重启和终态策略；`acquireUnit` 抛出的错误以 `LAUNCH_FAILED` 报告，原始错误在 `cause` 上。停止的三段（应用收尾、正常退出、强制回收）各 5 秒。重启默认 `on-failure`，初始间隔 250 毫秒，倍数 2，最长 30 秒，60 秒内最多 5 次。默认终态策略是停在 `terminal`，直到显式调用 `restart()`；配置 `cooldown` 后会安排一次不阻止进程退出的重试。健康检查默认每 5 秒一次，单次限时 2 秒，连续 3 次失败判定为不健康。预算默认排队，排队最多等 30 秒，每秒最多发出 8 个名额。需要确定的时间行为时，传入自己的 scheduler。

symbols.name: createUnitBudget
symbols.purpose: Creates a shared runtime-neutral capacity and launch-rate budget. Pair with createSupervisor or profile constructors; retain leases until actual unit exit.
symbols.core:
An `IUnitBudget`; invalid numeric limits or parent-kind mismatch throw coded `INVALID_OPTION` before admission starts.
kind: Choose which kind of work this budget counts: processes, threads or coroutines, where a coroutine is a task running within the current runtime. Set kind when creating the budget so unrelated resource types do not share capacity. If parent is supplied, its kind must match; a mismatch makes construction throw TypeError.
maxUnits: Finite nonnegative integer local concurrency cap; zero admits no unit.
overflow: Explicit reject refuses full capacity immediately; queue waits in FIFO order.
Omitted: queues in the current implementation; set reject explicitly for immediate refusal.
Use reject for immediate overload feedback: full capacity returns full. queue waits in FIFO order until a slot or queueTimeoutMs; omission currently queues too. The parent-budget example queues for at most five seconds; the rate example rejects overload immediately.
queueTimeoutMs: Finite positive scheduler deadline for a queued acquisition; expiry is a queue-timeout result.
`30000` milliseconds for each acquisition.
launchRate: Sliding grant rate independent of concurrent capacity; false disables rate limiting.
`{ max: 8, windowMs: 1000 }` grants eight leases per second.
Disable launch-rate limiting while retaining concurrency limits.
Configure max and windowMs to limit rapid starts even after prior slots are released. false disables that sliding grant window but retains maxUnits. Omission allows eight grants in 1000 ms. The example permits four grants per second.
launchRate.max: Positive integer maximum successful grants in one sliding launch-rate window.
launchRate.windowMs: Finite positive scheduler length of the sliding grant-rate window.
parent: Optional matching-kind budget obtained from another createUnitBudget call; the lease composes both slots.
Absent: only local admission is applied.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
parameters: options: IUnitBudgetOptions<TKind>
symbols.returns: IUnitBudget<TKind>
overloadSignatures: export declare function createUnitBudget<TKind extends string>(options: IUnitBudgetOptions<TKind>): IUnitBudget<TKind>;

generation: Attempt generation used to correlate commands and events; it does not count successful restarts.

members.name: state
members.description: Current lifecycle state; changes are also published as `state` events.

members.name: generation
members.description: Number of the latest start attempt; a successful start identifies the serving unit.

members.name: start
members.description: Starts the unit, retrying through backoff, and resolves with a stable answer: `ready` with the unit, `stopped` (possibly with a budget rejection) or `terminal`. Unit failures never reject; only a disposed supervisor rejects. Calling it while ready or starting joins the same answer.

members.name: whenReady
members.description: Waits for the next stable answer without starting anything; `signal` abandons the wait.

members.name: stop
members.description: Stops the current attempt and unit through the bounded drain, exit and reap phases, then settles in `stopped`. It returns on time even if the unit ignores stop; that unit keeps its budget slot until it actually exits. Concurrent calls share one promise; `graceMs` shortens the drain phase.

members.name: kill
members.description: Immediately upgrades the original slot teardown; joiners retain the pending stop promise.

members.name: restart
members.description: Clears the failure window, stops the current unit and starts a fresh one, even from `terminal`.

members.name: replace
members.signature: replace(options?: { readonly strategy?: ReplaceStrategy; readonly spec?: TSpec; }): Promise<IReplaceOutcome>;
members.description: Replaces the serving unit, optionally with a new spec. `stop-then-start` (default) stops first; `start-then-switch` switches only after the new unit is ready, then stops the old one. A failed replacement resolves `failed` or `rejected` and leaves a still-serving old unit in place.

parameterDetails.name: options

members.name: dispose
members.description: Stops like `stop()` and closes the supervisor for good; later commands are rejected.

symbols.name: ISupervisorBaseOptions
symbols.purpose: Shared readiness, restart, drain and health policy used by every execution profile.
symbols.core:
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
Set ready when creating a handle does not yet make its service usable. Resolve after the handshake; rejection fails startup and follows restart policy. Omit it to accept launch completion as readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
Use on-failure to retry crashes but stop after normal completion. never disables automatic retries; always also restarts normal exits. Omission selects on-failure. The task follows the configured backoff when a startup attempt fails.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
Choose stay when an operator must intervene after restart exhaustion. cooldown reopens admission after afterMs. Omitting terminalPolicy keeps the stay behavior. Disposal permanently closes either policy.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
Set beforeTerminate to drain pending application work before termination. Resolve after flushing; rejection is reported and retirement continues. drainTimeoutMs, exitTimeoutMs and reapTimeoutMs bound separate phases. Omit the callback to skip draining; omitted phase limits are 5000 ms.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force. Explicitly unsupported exit observation reports EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE immediately; abandoned leases remain held until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
Set health for a service that can become unresponsive without exiting. check resolves on success; rejection or timeout counts toward failureThreshold. Reaching that threshold invalidates readiness. Omit health for no periodic checks; coroutine heartbeat cannot coexist with it.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
Keep required, the default, when requested capabilities must be enforced or monitored; weaker declarations fail construction. Choose best-effort only when weaker guarantees are acceptable. This coroutine cannot isolate faults, so its additional fault-isolation requirement appears in degraded diagnostics.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.

symbols.name: ISupervisorOptions
symbols.purpose: Custom unit construction policy joining runtime adapter, profile and application ownership.
symbols.core:
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
Set ready when creating a handle does not yet make its service usable. Resolve after the handshake; rejection fails startup and follows restart policy. Omit it to accept launch completion as readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
Use on-failure to retry crashes but stop after normal completion. never disables automatic retries; always also restarts normal exits. Omission selects on-failure. The task follows the configured backoff when a startup attempt fails.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
Choose stay when an operator must intervene after restart exhaustion. cooldown reopens admission after afterMs. Omitting terminalPolicy keeps the stay behavior. Disposal permanently closes either policy.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
Set beforeTerminate to drain pending application work before termination. Resolve after flushing; rejection is reported and retirement continues. drainTimeoutMs, exitTimeoutMs and reapTimeoutMs bound separate phases. Omit the callback to skip draining; omitted phase limits are 5000 ms.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force. Explicitly unsupported exit observation reports EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE immediately; abandoned leases remain held until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
Set health for a service that can become unresponsive without exiting. check resolves on success; rejection or timeout counts toward failureThreshold. Reaching that threshold invalidates readiness. Omit health for no periodic checks; coroutine heartbeat cannot coexist with it.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
Keep required, the default, when requested capabilities must be enforced or monitored; weaker declarations fail construction. Choose best-effort only when weaker guarantees are acceptable. This coroutine cannot isolate faults, so its additional fault-isolation requirement appears in degraded diagnostics.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
profile: Application-supplied `IUnitProfile` owns validation, required capabilities, termination and exit classification.
hooks: Optional `ISupervisionHooks` supplied by the outer adapter for adoption, attachment and diagnostics.
Absent: no adapter extension hooks run.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.

symbols.name: IUnitBudget
symbols.purpose: Application-owned shared admission budget; closing admission does not release live leases.
symbols.core:
kind: Unit kind chosen at budget construction; parent and supervisor kinds must match it.
acquire: Requests a FIFO lease respecting capacity, rate, parent and cancellation. It reserves local capacity before waiting for the parent; reservation is not a started unit. Refusal is data and composite release returns parent before child.
acquire.signal: Optional caller cancellation signal; aborted requests return the aborted reason.
An `IBudgetOutcome`; granted leases must be released after actual exit.
tryAcquire: Attempts immediate admission without joining the wait queue; existing queued callers have precedence.
A synchronous granted lease or stable rejection reason.
inUse: Number of occupied local unit leases; queued requests are counted separately.
pending: Unresolved acquire calls including the active FIFO queue head.
closed: Whether admission has permanently closed; existing occupied leases remain valid.
close: Rejects waiting and future acquisitions; existing leases remain occupied until their owners release them.
Admission is closed; repeated close calls have no further effect.
symbols.advanced: Share a concurrency ceiling across several supervisors of the same kind.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

kind: Choose which kind of work this budget counts: processes, threads or coroutines, where a coroutine is a task running within the current runtime. Set kind when creating the budget so unrelated resource types do not share capacity. If parent is supplied, its kind must match; a mismatch makes construction throw TypeError.
maxUnits: Finite nonnegative integer local concurrency cap; zero admits no unit.
overflow: Explicit reject refuses full capacity immediately; queue waits in FIFO order.
Omitted: queues in the current implementation; set reject explicitly for immediate refusal.
Use reject for immediate overload feedback: full capacity returns full. queue waits in FIFO order until a slot or queueTimeoutMs; omission currently queues too. The parent-budget example queues for at most five seconds; the rate example rejects overload immediately.
queueTimeoutMs: Finite positive scheduler deadline for a queued acquisition; expiry is a queue-timeout result.
`30000` milliseconds for each acquisition.
launchRate: Sliding grant rate independent of concurrent capacity; false disables rate limiting.
`{ max: 8, windowMs: 1000 }` grants eight leases per second.
Disable launch-rate limiting while retaining concurrency limits.
Configure max and windowMs to limit rapid starts even after prior slots are released. false disables that sliding grant window but retains maxUnits. Omission allows eight grants in 1000 ms. The example permits four grants per second.
launchRate.max: Positive integer maximum successful grants in one sliding launch-rate window.
launchRate.windowMs: Finite positive scheduler length of the sliding grant-rate window.
parent: Optional matching-kind budget obtained from another createUnitBudget call; the lease composes both slots.
Absent: only local admission is applied.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.

symbols.name: SupervisionErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Stable semantic errors from supervisor construction and contained execution failures. Values are stable public contract identifiers; use the matching table entries below.
symbols.core:
invalidOption: `INVALID_OPTION`: invalid constructor, specification or command option; correct the named field before retrying.
capabilityUnsupported: `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`: required capability lacks a sufficient guarantee; change launcher or isolation policy.
launchFailed: LAUNCH_FAILED: preacquisition, launch, attachment or readiness failed. An acquireUnit failure before lease acquisition still returns a controlled failed readiness outcome and follows the configured failure policy; inspect phase and preserved cause.
startupTimeout: STARTUP_TIMEOUT: startup missed its deadline. Bounded retirement advances to the configured backoff, stopped or terminal policy without leaking a temporary terminal event or leaving starting stuck; readiness receives a stable failed result.
exitUnexpected: `EXIT_UNEXPECTED`: unexpected actual exit; inspect native status and original cause.
unhealthy: `UNHEALTHY`: health failures crossed the threshold; the generation is invalidated.
resourceLimitExceeded: `RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: resource monitoring observed a limit breach; inspect the limit detail.
reapTimeout: `REAP_TIMEOUT`: observable exit or pending launch exceeded its recovery deadline; the lease remains occupied.
exitUnobservable: `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE`: the launcher explicitly declares exit-observation unsupported. Force reports immediately with kind, generation and capability, publishes abandoned, and retains the lease until actual exit. Choose an observable launcher when an exit receipt is required.
supervisionExhausted: `SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED`: restart window exhausted; inspect terminal error before explicit restart.
scopeClosed: `SCOPE_CLOSED`: a unit-producing command ran during disposal; wait for completion.
scopeTerminal: `SCOPE_TERMINAL`: a unit-producing command ran after disposal; create a new supervisor.
heartbeatMissed: `HEARTBEAT_MISSED`: a coroutine heartbeat became stale; inspect cooperative task progress.
orphanReclaimFailed: ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED: registry listing or a per-record probe/termination/removal failed. Listing failure is collected and reported with detail.step=list and original cause; no record is touched. Failed records remain available for retry.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.

symbols.name: createCoroutineSupervisor
symbols.purpose: Supervises a cooperative task or async iterator without native process isolation. Task cancellation is cooperative; an unending task keeps its budget lease after bounded recovery.
symbols.core:
An `ICoroutineSupervisor`; invalid task or simultaneous heartbeat and health policies throw `INVALID_OPTION`.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
Set ready when creating a handle does not yet make its service usable. Resolve after the handshake; rejection fails startup and follows restart policy. Omit it to accept launch completion as readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
Use on-failure to retry crashes but stop after normal completion. never disables automatic retries; always also restarts normal exits. Omission selects on-failure. The task follows the configured backoff when a startup attempt fails.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
Choose stay when an operator must intervene after restart exhaustion. cooldown reopens admission after afterMs. Omitting terminalPolicy keeps the stay behavior. Disposal permanently closes either policy.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
Set beforeTerminate to drain pending application work before termination. Resolve after flushing; rejection is reported and retirement continues. drainTimeoutMs, exitTimeoutMs and reapTimeoutMs bound separate phases. Omit the callback to skip draining; omitted phase limits are 5000 ms.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force. Explicitly unsupported exit observation reports EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE immediately; abandoned leases remain held until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
Set health for a service that can become unresponsive without exiting. check resolves on success; rejection or timeout counts toward failureThreshold. Reaching that threshold invalidates readiness. Omit health for no periodic checks; coroutine heartbeat cannot coexist with it.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
Keep required, the default, when requested capabilities must be enforced or monitored; weaker declarations fail construction. Choose best-effort only when weaker guarantees are acceptable. This coroutine cannot isolate faults, so its additional fault-isolation requirement appears in degraded diagnostics.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
heartbeat: Optional heartbeat-age watchdog observing task progress rather than native health.
Absent: no heartbeat watchdog is installed.
heartbeat.timeoutMs: Finite positive maximum scheduler age since the last explicit or iterator heartbeat.
heartbeat.intervalMs: Positive scheduler interval between heartbeat-age observations.
The configured heartbeat.timeoutMs duration.
heartbeat.failureThreshold: Consecutive stale heartbeat observations required before invalidating the coroutine.
`1`; the first stale observation fails.
parameters: options: ICoroutineSupervisorOptions<TPort>
symbols.returns: ICoroutineSupervisor<TPort>

symbols.purpose: Application-owned command controller for one active execution unit and bounded restart policy.
symbols.core:
state: Current lifecycle state read synchronously without launching or checking the unit.
generation: Attempt generation used to correlate commands and events; it does not count successful restarts.
start: Starts or joins readiness; construction creates no native unit. Startup timeout follows the configured failure policy, while acquireUnit rejection becomes LAUNCH_FAILED with cause even before a lease exists.
An `IReadyOutcome`; disposal rejects with `SCOPE_CLOSED` or `SCOPE_TERMINAL`.
whenReady: Observes stable readiness without starting a new command; cancellation rejects with the caller signal reason.
whenReady.signal: Optional application cancellation signal; abort affects this wait only.
The current `IReadyOutcome`, or rejection on cancellation.
stop: Drains and retires current work; concurrent calls share the pending stop Promise, and the supervisor can later start again.
stop.options: Optional `ISupervisorStopOptions` from the caller; graceMs overrides application drain only.
Resolves after bounded teardown; abandoned actual work retains its lease.
kill: Upgrades the existing teardown to force immediately; joining callers keep the original pending stop Promise.
Resolves after the same bounded stop sequence.
restart: Resets recent restart failures, retires the active unit and launches a fresh attempt.
Readiness outcome for the fresh attempt; disposal rejects with a scope error.
replace: Replaces an active unit with the same or a new spec; invalid strategy throws `INVALID_OPTION` before changing the serving unit.
replace.options: Replacement options: default stop-then-start and current spec. Start-then-switch needs another slot; the serving unit remains owned by its active slot after startup attempt completion. Only candidate readiness and the switched event permit cancelling the old task.
`IReplaceOutcome` reports replacement, admission refusal, or failure without hiding the original error.
inspect: Reads diagnostics without sampling native resources or modifying lifecycle state.
An `ISupervisorSnapshot` of current state and contained failures.
subscribe: Registers a synchronous event observer; it receives `ISupervisorEvent` changes and observer throws are reported.
subscribe.listener: Application callback receives a discriminated event, returns void synchronously, and should not throw.
Idempotent removal function for this observer only.
dispose: Closes admission permanently and joins bounded retirement; repeated in-flight calls share one disposal Promise.
Resolves when disposal reaches its terminal state; future unit-producing commands reject.
symbols.advanced: Keep a background task alive and release it at application shutdown.

members.name: state
members.description: Current lifecycle state; changes are also published as `state` events.

members.name: generation
members.description: Number of the latest start attempt; a successful start identifies the serving unit.

members.name: start
members.description: Starts the unit, retrying through backoff, and resolves with a stable answer: `ready` with the unit, `stopped` (possibly with a budget rejection) or `terminal`. Unit failures never reject; only a disposed supervisor rejects. Calling it while ready or starting joins the same answer.

members.name: whenReady
members.description: Waits for the next stable answer without starting anything; `signal` abandons the wait.

members.name: stop
members.description: Stops the current attempt and unit through the bounded drain, exit and reap phases, then settles in `stopped`. It returns on time even if the unit ignores stop; that unit keeps its budget slot until it actually exits. Concurrent calls share one promise; `graceMs` shortens the drain phase.

members.name: kill
members.description: Immediately upgrades the original slot teardown; joiners retain the pending stop promise.

members.name: restart
members.description: Clears the failure window, stops the current unit and starts a fresh one, even from `terminal`.

members.name: replace
members.signature: replace(options?: { readonly strategy?: ReplaceStrategy; readonly spec?: TSpec; }): Promise<IReplaceOutcome>;
members.description: Replaces the serving unit, optionally with a new spec. `stop-then-start` (default) stops first; `start-then-switch` switches only after the new unit is ready, then stops the old one. A failed replacement resolves `failed` or `rejected` and leaves a still-serving old unit in place.

members.name: inspect
members.description: Reads state, last exit, failure window, health and degradation without side effects.

members.name: subscribe
members.description: Registers an event listener and returns its unsubscribe function; listener errors are reported.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Stops like `stop()` and closes the supervisor for good; later commands are rejected.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Application-owned command controller for one active execution unit and bounded restart policy.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import ICoroutineSupervisor from @migaia/supervision/coroutine, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use ICoroutineSupervisor when its type contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when ICoroutineSupervisor does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained type example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
state: Current lifecycle state read synchronously without launching or checking the unit.
generation: Attempt generation used to correlate commands and events; it does not count successful restarts.
start: Starts or joins readiness; construction creates no native unit. Startup timeout follows the configured failure policy, while acquireUnit rejection becomes LAUNCH_FAILED with cause even before a lease exists.
An `IReadyOutcome`; disposal rejects with `SCOPE_CLOSED` or `SCOPE_TERMINAL`.
whenReady: Observes stable readiness without starting a new command; cancellation rejects with the caller signal reason.
whenReady.signal: Optional application cancellation signal; abort affects this wait only.
The current `IReadyOutcome`, or rejection on cancellation.
stop: Drains and retires current work; concurrent calls share the pending stop Promise, and the supervisor can later start again.
stop.options: Optional `ISupervisorStopOptions` from the caller; graceMs overrides application drain only.
Resolves after bounded teardown; abandoned actual work retains its lease.
kill: Upgrades the existing teardown to force immediately; joining callers keep the original pending stop Promise.
Resolves after the same bounded stop sequence.
restart: Resets recent restart failures, retires the active unit and launches a fresh attempt.
Readiness outcome for the fresh attempt; disposal rejects with a scope error.
replace: Replaces an active unit with the same or a new spec; invalid strategy throws `INVALID_OPTION` before changing the serving unit.
replace.options: Replacement options: default stop-then-start and current spec. Start-then-switch needs another slot; the serving unit remains owned by its active slot after startup attempt completion. Only candidate readiness and the switched event permit cancelling the old task.
`IReplaceOutcome` reports replacement, admission refusal, or failure without hiding the original error.
inspect: Reads diagnostics without sampling native resources or modifying lifecycle state.
An `ISupervisorSnapshot` of current state and contained failures.
subscribe: Registers a synchronous event observer; it receives `ISupervisorEvent` changes and observer throws are reported.
subscribe.listener: Application callback receives a discriminated event, returns void synchronously, and should not throw.
Idempotent removal function for this observer only.
dispose: Closes admission permanently and joins bounded retirement; repeated in-flight calls share one disposal Promise.
Resolves when disposal reaches its terminal state; future unit-producing commands reject.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content: Keep a background task alive and release it at application shutdown.

symbols.name: ICoroutineSupervisorOptions
symbols.purpose: Cooperative task policy with optional heartbeat monitoring; heartbeat and health cannot coexist.
symbols.core:
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
Set ready when creating a handle does not yet make its service usable. Resolve after the handshake; rejection fails startup and follows restart policy. Omit it to accept launch completion as readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
Use on-failure to retry crashes but stop after normal completion. never disables automatic retries; always also restarts normal exits. Omission selects on-failure. The task follows the configured backoff when a startup attempt fails.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
Choose stay when an operator must intervene after restart exhaustion. cooldown reopens admission after afterMs. Omitting terminalPolicy keeps the stay behavior. Disposal permanently closes either policy.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
Set beforeTerminate to drain pending application work before termination. Resolve after flushing; rejection is reported and retirement continues. drainTimeoutMs, exitTimeoutMs and reapTimeoutMs bound separate phases. Omit the callback to skip draining; omitted phase limits are 5000 ms.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force. Explicitly unsupported exit observation reports EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE immediately; abandoned leases remain held until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
Set health for a service that can become unresponsive without exiting. check resolves on success; rejection or timeout counts toward failureThreshold. Reaching that threshold invalidates readiness. Omit health for no periodic checks; coroutine heartbeat cannot coexist with it.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
Keep required, the default, when requested capabilities must be enforced or monitored; weaker declarations fail construction. Choose best-effort only when weaker guarantees are acceptable. This coroutine cannot isolate faults, so its additional fault-isolation requirement appears in degraded diagnostics.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
heartbeat: Optional heartbeat-age watchdog observing task progress rather than native health.
Absent: no heartbeat watchdog is installed.
heartbeat.timeoutMs: Finite positive maximum scheduler age since the last explicit or iterator heartbeat.
heartbeat.intervalMs: Positive scheduler interval between heartbeat-age observations.
The configured heartbeat.timeoutMs duration.
heartbeat.failureThreshold: Consecutive stale heartbeat observations required before invalidating the coroutine.
`1`; the first stale observation fails.

symbols.name: createParentLossGuard
symbols.purpose: Creates an idempotent parent-loss trigger that runs one cancellable shutdown and requests exit code zero on success or one on failure or deadline.
symbols.core:
options: Application object with shutdown(signal), exit(code), report(error), optional positive graceMs (5000), and scheduler (systemScheduler). Shutdown may be async; throws are reported then forced exit is requested.
A trigger controller with trigger(reason?) and triggered. Repeated triggers do nothing; deadline aborts shutdown with the first reason.
shutdown: Application shutdown callback receives the guard cancellation signal and returns a PromiseLike resolving after cleanup. A throw or rejection is reported, then requests forced exit.
Provide the cleanup to run once on parent loss. Resolve within graceMs for exit zero; throw or reject for exit one and reporting. This callback is required.
exit: Application synchronous exit callback receives ParentLossExitCode zero on shutdown completion or one on failure/deadline; its own throws propagate.
Provide the child runtime exit operation. Zero means cleanup completed; one means failure or deadline. Here a recorder shows the request. The callback is required and its own throws propagate.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
graceMs: Finite positive shutdown deadline in scheduler milliseconds; expiry aborts shutdown before requesting forced exit.
`5000` milliseconds for one shutdown attempt.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Creates an idempotent parent-loss trigger that runs one cancellable shutdown and requests exit code zero on success or one on failure or deadline.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import createParentLossGuard from @migaia/supervision/process, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use createParentLossGuard when its function contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when createParentLossGuard does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained function example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
options: Application object with shutdown(signal), exit(code), report(error), optional positive graceMs (5000), and scheduler (systemScheduler). Shutdown may be async; throws are reported then forced exit is requested.
A trigger controller with trigger(reason?) and triggered. Repeated triggers do nothing; deadline aborts shutdown with the first reason.
shutdown: Application shutdown callback receives the guard cancellation signal and returns a PromiseLike resolving after cleanup. A throw or rejection is reported, then requests forced exit.
Provide the cleanup to run once on parent loss. Resolve within graceMs for exit zero; throw or reject for exit one and reporting. This callback is required.
exit: Application synchronous exit callback receives ParentLossExitCode zero on shutdown completion or one on failure/deadline; its own throws propagate.
Provide the child runtime exit operation. Zero means cleanup completed; one means failure or deadline. Here a recorder shows the request. The callback is required and its own throws propagate.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
graceMs: Finite positive shutdown deadline in scheduler milliseconds; expiry aborts shutdown before requesting forced exit.
`5000` milliseconds for one shutdown attempt.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.

symbols.name: createPrewarmPool
symbols.purpose: Maintains a bounded non-restarting pool of idle native processes. Pair with createProcessSupervisor to transfer ready handles and occupied leases without cold startup.
symbols.core:
An `IPrewarmPool`; every idle process consumes the same shared process budget, and disposal retires remaining owned entries.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
Keep required, the default, when requested capabilities must be enforced or monitored; weaker declarations fail construction. Choose best-effort only when weaker guarantees are acceptable. This coroutine cannot isolate faults, so its additional fault-isolation requirement appears in degraded diagnostics.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
registry: Application durable record port and namespace for recovering prior-run process identities.
Absent: no durable records or orphan recovery.
registry.port: Application storage implementing `IProcessRegistry`; add and removal follow actual process ownership.
registry.namespace: Application chosen isolation name; recovery lists only records in this namespace.
usage: Native resource sampling policy used when process memory or CPU limits are monitored.
Absent: samples use interval and threshold defaults.
usage.intervalMs: Finite positive scheduler interval for native process resource samples. Both supervisor and prewarm pool reject zero/nonfinite intervals and nonpositive or unsafe failure thresholds as RangeError/INVALID_OPTION.
`1000` milliseconds between samples.
usage.failureThreshold: Positive safe-integer count of consecutive sampleUsage rejections before the process is unhealthy. A successful sample resets this count; a successful sample exceeding a monitored limit terminates immediately.
`3` consecutive sampleUsage rejections, not three successful over-limit samples.
wallClock: Epoch clock supplied by the application for durable launch timestamps; not used for deadlines.
`systemWallClock`; uses host epoch time.
size: Nonnegative integer target of ready idle processes, each retaining one shared budget lease.
idleTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum idle retention before an unused prewarm handle is retired; zero expires immediately.
`60000` milliseconds of idle retention.
exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force. Explicitly unsupported exit observation reports EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE immediately; abandoned leases remain held until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
parameters: options: IPrewarmPoolOptions<THandle>
symbols.returns: IPrewarmPool<THandle>

symbols.name: createProcessSupervisor
symbols.purpose: Supervises shell-free native processes through an injected launcher, with optional resource monitoring, bounded output tails and durable ownership records.
symbols.core:
An `IProcessSupervisor`; invalid closed specification throws `INVALID_OPTION`, unsupported capabilities fail before launch.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
Set ready when creating a handle does not yet make its service usable. Resolve after the handshake; rejection fails startup and follows restart policy. Omit it to accept launch completion as readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
Use on-failure to retry crashes but stop after normal completion. never disables automatic retries; always also restarts normal exits. Omission selects on-failure. The task follows the configured backoff when a startup attempt fails.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
Choose stay when an operator must intervene after restart exhaustion. cooldown reopens admission after afterMs. Omitting terminalPolicy keeps the stay behavior. Disposal permanently closes either policy.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
Set beforeTerminate to drain pending application work before termination. Resolve after flushing; rejection is reported and retirement continues. drainTimeoutMs, exitTimeoutMs and reapTimeoutMs bound separate phases. Omit the callback to skip draining; omitted phase limits are 5000 ms.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force. Explicitly unsupported exit observation reports EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE immediately; abandoned leases remain held until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Supervises shell-free native processes through an injected launcher, with optional resource monitoring, bounded output tails and durable ownership records.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import createProcessSupervisor from @migaia/supervision/process, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use createProcessSupervisor when its function contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when createProcessSupervisor does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained function example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

An `IProcessSupervisor`; invalid closed specification throws `INVALID_OPTION`, unsupported capabilities fail before launch.

report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
Supply a synchronous nonthrowing sink for contained failures. A failed drain is reported while retirement continues. Reporting does not retry work or complete shutdown; this callback is required.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
Set ready when creating a handle does not yet make its service usable. Resolve after the handshake; rejection fails startup and follows restart policy. Omit it to accept launch completion as readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
Use on-failure to retry crashes but stop after normal completion. never disables automatic retries; always also restarts normal exits. Omission selects on-failure. The task follows the configured backoff when a startup attempt fails.

`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.

restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.

restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.

terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
